description: The Accounting major provides students with the technical, analytical, and communication skills necessary for success in this diverse and dynamic field. Accountants are the professionals who record, report, and analyze financial information and serve as advisors to business leaders. Students gain a solid foundation in core business subjects and complete advanced coursework in financial reporting, auditing, taxation, and accounting information systems. The program prepares graduates for various career paths, including public accounting, corporate accounting, management, and government. It also provides the educational requirements for professional certifications like the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and Certified Management Accountant (CMA).
Accreditation status: The Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business). The accounting program has also earned supplemental AACSB Accounting Accreditation.

description: The BFA in Acting is a professional preparatory program for the student who intends to pursue a career as an actor in the professional theatre. The program provides the student with the fundamental skills and techniques of acting, voice, and movement while also providing a broad-based education in the liberal arts.
Accreditation status: The Department of Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

description: Actuarial science is the study of the financial risk of uncertain future events. Actuaries use their knowledge of mathematics, statistics, and finance to help businesses and individuals make informed decisions about their financial futures. Purdue’s Actuarial Science program is a joint program between the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics. It is recognized by the Society of Actuaries as a Center of Actuarial Excellence.
Accreditation status: Recognized by the Society of Actuaries as a Center of Actuarial Excellence

description: This minor is designed to provide students with the opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of the global technological environment and its impact on society. Students will be able to: Demonstrate an understanding of the impact of technology on society and the environment in a global context. Demonstrate an understanding of the global technological environment and its impact on society.

Aeronautical and astronautical engineering is a field that deals with the design, development, testing, and production of aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems and equipment. The curriculum provides a thorough preparation in the basic sciences, engineering sciences, and the social and humanistic areas. The professional courses provide students with a strong background in the fundamental areas of aerospace engineering: aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, dynamics and control, and systems design.
Accreditation status: The Aeronautical and Astronautical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: Aeronautical engineering technology (AET) graduates apply engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development, manufacture, and maintenance of aircraft and their systems. Graduates of this program are typically employed in the fields of aircraft manufacturing, maintenance, and systems testing.
Accreditation status: The Aeronautical Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Aerospace Financial Analysis major is designed to prepare students for careers in the financial and business sectors of the aerospace and aviation industries. This program combines a strong foundation in aviation and aerospace with business and financial analysis skills. Students will gain an understanding of the aerospace industry, including its history, regulations, and technological advancements, while also developing proficiency in financial modeling, investment analysis, and risk management. Graduates will be equipped to work in a variety of roles, such as financial analysts, consultants, and managers within aerospace companies, airlines, and government agencies.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI)

description: The Aerospace Studies minor is available to all students who meet the course requirements. It provides a unique opportunity for students to gain a broader understanding of the Department of the Air Force and its role in national security. Students will explore leadership and management principles, global security issues, and the evolution of air and space power.

African American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the African-American experience in the United States, as well as the experiences of people of African descent throughout the African Diaspora (e.g., in the Caribbean, South America, and Europe). It offers students a variety of perspectives through which to examine these experiences, including history, literature, sociology, political science, and the arts.

African American Studies is an interdisciplinary program that offers a comprehensive approach to the study of the history, culture, and social organization of people of African descent. Drawing from the humanities and social sciences, the program helps students understand the African American experience from historical and contemporary perspectives. Students develop skills in research, critical thinking and communication, which prepare them for careers in law, public policy, education, social services and the arts.

Concentration name: Agribusiness Management, Agricultural Marketing, Commodity Marketing, Finance, Real Estate, Sales and Marketing, Value Added and Food Systems
description: Students in the Agribusiness major receive a strong foundation in management, marketing, finance, and data analysis. The Agribusiness degree provides students with the management and analytical tools required for a successful career in a wide variety of agribusinesses, including firms in the food, fiber, and biofuels supply chains. Students take courses in the College of Agriculture and the School of Business.

The agricultural communication major is offered by the Department of Agricultural Sciences Education and Communication. It is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in agricultural journalism, broadcasting, public relations, advertising, or marketing communication. Students may tailor the curriculum to meet their career goals through a wide variety of communication electives and a specific area of interest in agriculture or the environment.

Concentration name: Applied Agricultural Economics, Data Science, Policy and Pre-Law, Quantitative Analysis
description: The Agricultural Economics major provides students with a broad background in the business and economics of the food and fiber industry. Students in Agricultural Economics will develop a strong foundation in economic theory, quantitative methods, and the application of these tools to the agricultural and food sectors. This major prepares students for careers in management, marketing, finance, and policy analysis.

Students in the Agricultural Education program prepare for careers as teachers of agriculture in junior and senior high schools. The program also prepares graduates for careers in agricultural industry, non-formal education, and the Cooperative Extension Service. Students complete coursework in all areas of agriculture and in education. Graduates are eligible to receive a license to teach agriculture in the State of Indiana. Graduates may also be licensed to teach in other states.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

Concentration name: Machine Systems Engineering and Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering
description: Agricultural Engineering (AE) is an engineering discipline that applies engineering principles to the production, processing, and distribution of agricultural products and the management of natural resources. Agricultural engineers are trained in the basic mathematical and physical sciences. Their specialty includes a sequence of engineering science and design courses. Agricultural engineers are unique in that they apply engineering principles to biologically based systems. In the sophomore year, students begin to focus on one of two concentrations in the major. Both concentrations culminate in a capstone senior design sequence. Machine Systems Engineering concentration focuses on the design and development of machines used in the agricultural, construction, forestry and landscape industries. Machine systems engineers design, test and evaluate machines such as tractors and implements, combines, lawn and garden equipment, and construction and off-road equipment. Students are trained in power and energy systems, electronic sensors and control systems, fluid power, and machine design. Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering (ENRE) concentration focuses on the application of engineering principles and techniques to solve problems involving the environment and our natural resources. ENRE engineers work to improve water quality and protect our soil, air and water resources. Students are trained in hydrology, soil and water conservation, irrigation and drainage, and ecological engineering. ENRE engineers often work in government agencies, consulting firms, and non-profit organizations.
Accreditation status: The Agricultural Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Agricultural Systems Management minor is for students who want to develop their knowledge and skills in managing technological systems for food, fiber, and natural resources.

Agricultural Systems Management (ASM) is for students who want to be solvers of technical problems for the global food and agricultural industry. The ASM program is a bridge between engineering and the end users of technologies. ASM graduates are professionals who manage technical systems such as machinery, agricultural production, and food processing systems. Students study a variety of topics including machine systems, soil and water systems, electricity and electronics, structural systems, and precision agriculture. Students also take several business courses to develop management and leadership skills. A professional internship is a requirement for the program. Students can select electives to focus on a particular area of interest such as data analytics, unmanned aerial systems, natural resources, or machine systems.

Concentration name: Agronomic Business and Marketing, Applied Meteorology and Climatology, Crop and Soil Management, International Agronomy, Plant Genetics and Breeding, Soil and Environmental Science
description: Agronomy is the science of managing the soil and the plant in such a way as to maximize the benefit of both. Students study the basic sciences and apply them to the production of food, feed, and fiber, and the management of land resources for environmental protection. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in the agribusiness sector, government agencies, and research organizations.

Air traffic controllers are responsible for the safe, orderly and efficient movement of aircraft in the National Airspace System. Purdue’s air traffic control (ATC) program is one of a select few in the nation that is part of the FAA’s Air Traffic Collegiate Training Initiative (AT-CTI). You will learn about the technology, regulations and procedures used to manage air traffic in our National Airspace System. You’ll use state-of-the-art simulators to gain hands-on experience in various ATC environments, including tower, terminal and en route operations.
Accreditation status: The School of Aviation and Transportation Technology is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

description: The Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance minor is intended for students in the Aeronautical Engineering Technology and Aviation Management majors who desire to obtain the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) mechanic certificate. The A&P certificate is a requirement for many entry-level positions in the aviation industry.

Modern aviation needs managers with a holistic view of the entire aviation ecosystem. The Airline Management and Operations (AMO) major focuses on the business, operational, and management aspects of the airline industry. Students study the core principles of airline operations, revenue management, fleet planning, and crew scheduling. They gain insights into the regulatory framework, safety management systems, and the economic factors that drive airline decision-making. Through case studies and projects, students learn to optimize airline performance while ensuring safety and efficiency. This major prepares graduates for diverse leadership roles within airlines, from network planning and operations control to customer service management and regulatory compliance.

The American Studies Minor provides an interdisciplinary approach to the study of American culture, past and present. It is designed to complement a student’s major by providing a broader perspective on the American experience.

American Studies is the study of the people, places and ideas that comprise the United States. It involves a critical look at the American experience from various perspectives and involves several different academic departments. Students can explore such diverse topics as popular culture, film, literature, history and social justice. Because American Studies is interdisciplinary, students have the flexibility to tailor their education to their specific interests.

The Animal Science minor is designed for students who want to develop a basic understanding of the animal sciences to supplement their major program of study. The minor is available to any student at Purdue University with the exception of those majoring in Animal Sciences.

Concentration name: Agribusiness, Animal BioHealth/Pre-Professional, Behavioral Well-being, Biosciences, and Production and Management
description: Animal sciences is the study of animals that live alongside humans. Most often, that means livestock species (beef and dairy cattle, poultry, sheep, pigs) and companion animals. Animal science students study everything from the cell to the whole animal and how to best manage these animals to ensure they are healthy and productive. Students in the animal sciences major gain a foundation in biology and the physical sciences. Students also choose one of five concentrations to specialize in: Agribusiness, Animal BioHealth/Pre-Professional, Behavioral Well-being, Biosciences, or Production and Management.

The Animation and Visual Effects major focuses on the creative side of the animation process. Students will learn the principles of animation, character design, storytelling, and visual effects for film and games. The program integrates traditional art techniques with industry-standard software to prepare students for careers in the entertainment and media industries.
Accreditation status: National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

description: The Anthropology minor is designed to provide students with a general introduction to the four fields of the discipline: sociocultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. It offers students an opportunity to explore the diversity of human cultures, past and present, and the biological foundations of humanity.

Concentration name: Applied Anthropology, Environmental Anthropology
description: Anthropology is the study of human diversity across time and space. It is a holistic discipline, which means that anthropologists study all aspects of human life, including our biology, our history, our language, and our culture. The Anthropology major at Purdue University provides students with a broad background in the four fields of anthropology: socio-cultural anthropology, archaeology, biological anthropology, and linguistic anthropology. Students also have the opportunity to specialize in particular areas of interest through elective coursework and research opportunities.

The Applied Agricultural Economics major is for students who want to study the principles and concepts of economics and how they are applied to the food system, the environment, and the world. This major provides students with a strong background in economic theory and the quantitative tools needed to analyze real-world problems. Students will learn about agricultural marketing, resource economics, policy analysis, and international development.

The B.S. degree in Applied Leadership is a degree-completion program for students who have completed an Associate of Science (AS) or Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degree in a technical or professional field. The program is designed to provide students with the leadership and management skills needed to advance in their careers. Students will learn about organizational behavior, leadership theory, human resource management, and project management. The program is offered at several locations throughout Indiana and online.

The Applied Meteorology and Climatology major provides a foundation for students who want to become professionals in the fields of operational meteorology or applied climatology. Students will gain experience in the areas of weather and climate analysis, observation, and forecasting. The curriculum is designed to meet the requirements for employment as a meteorologist with the National Weather Service and other government agencies, and for employment as a meteorologist in the private sector.

Concentration name: Applied Physics, Atmospheric/Planetary, Business, Computer Science, Geology, Geophysics, or Physical Chemistry
description: The Applied Physics major is for students who wish to pursue a career in an area of applied physics or in an interdisciplinary field. It is also an excellent program for students who wish to enter the job market immediately after graduation. The curriculum for the Applied Physics major includes the core physics courses of the Physics major, but replaces some of the more advanced elective courses with a concentration of 12-18 credit hours in a specific area of applied physics or in a related field. Students may choose from among several established concentrations, such as atmospheric/planetary science, business, computer science, geology/geophysics, and physical chemistry, or may design their own concentration.

The Bachelor of Science with a major in applied statistics provides students with a strong background in statistical methods and their applications in a variety of fields. This program is designed to prepare students for careers in business, industry, government, and healthcare, and for graduate study in statistics or related fields. Students learn to use statistical software, analyze data, and interpret results to make informed decisions. Upon completion of this degree, students will be able to demonstrate a solid foundation in statistical theory, apply statistical methods to analyze data from various fields, use statistical software for data analysis, and communicate statistical results effectively.

Concentration name: Marine and Freshwater Biology; Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences
description: Students in the aquatic sciences major choose between two concentrations: marine and freshwater biology or fisheries and aquatic sciences. The marine and freshwater biology concentration provides a strong foundation in the biology and ecology of aquatic systems and the organisms that inhabit them. Students learn about the physiological, ecological, and behavioral adaptations that allow organisms to survive and thrive in aquatic environments. The fisheries and aquatic sciences concentration provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to manage and conserve fish and other aquatic organisms. Students learn about fish biology, ecology, and management, as well as the physical and chemical properties of aquatic systems and how they affect aquatic life.

The Arabic Language and Culture minor is designed to provide students with a basic proficiency in the Arabic language and a broad understanding of the culture and history of the Arabic-speaking world.

The Architectural Engineering Minor is designed for students who want to develop a background in the design and construction of buildings and their systems. Students take courses in architectural design, building systems, and construction management.

The Art and Design Studio minor allows students to pursue creative interests in various studio disciplines, including ceramics, drawing, painting, photography, printmaking, and sculpture. This minor provides students with the opportunity to develop their artistic skills and explore personal expression through a structured sequence of studio courses.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

description: The Art History minor is designed for students who are interested in the history of art and who wish to complement their major field of study with a concentration in this area. The minor provides a broad overview of the history of art, as well as the opportunity to pursue more specialized coursework in specific periods and styles.

The program in Art History provides students with a broad knowledge of the history of art and design from around the world. In addition to gaining a deep understanding of specific periods, cultures, and media, students develop skills in visual analysis, critical thinking, research, and writing. The curriculum prepares students for careers in museums, galleries, auction houses, and cultural organizations, as well as for graduate study in art history and related fields.

Concentration name: AI in Health, AI in Modern Society, AI in Philosophy, Autonomous Systems, Foundations of AI, Mathematical and Computational Foundations of AI
description: The Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence is a joint degree program between the College of Liberal Arts, the College of Science, and the Purdue Polytechnic Institute. This program will offer students a choice between three majors, based on their individual interests and career goals. Each major will have a common core of courses and specialized courses. Students who complete this degree will be able to: Use foundational knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence (AI) to solve problems across a range of AI contexts. Effectively use data to inform AI models and generate and apply AI solutions to real-world problems. Develop AI systems that demonstrate an understanding of ethical and societal implications of AI.

Asian American Studies at Purdue University is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the histories, experiences, and cultures of people of Asian descent in the United States. Our courses provide students with a foundational understanding of the diversity within Asian American communities and the historical and contemporary issues they face.

The Asian Studies program offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the history, politics, religion, philosophy, and cultures of Asia. This program provides students with a foundational understanding of Asian societies and prepares them for further study or for careers in a globalized world.

The Asian Studies program provides students with a broad-based knowledge of Asian cultures, history, politics, and languages. Students select courses from a variety of disciplines, including anthropology, art history, history, philosophy, political science, and sociology. The major requires the study of an Asian language (Chinese, Japanese, or Korean) and offers opportunities for study abroad in Asia.

The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers an Astronomy major for students who are interested in the study of the universe, from the solar system to the most distant galaxies. It provides a solid foundation in both the theoretical and observational aspects of modern astronomy and astrophysics. The curriculum includes courses in physics, mathematics, and computer science, as well as specialized courses in astronomy and astrophysics. Students will have the opportunity to participate in research projects with faculty members, which can lead to publications in scientific journals.

Atmospheric Science is the study of the Earth’s atmosphere and the processes that cause what we know as weather. Most atmospheric scientists work to improve our understanding and forecasting of weather and climate. Students in atmospheric science will develop a strong background in physics and mathematics to understand the physical and chemical processes that govern the atmosphere. The Atmospheric Science program at Purdue University meets the requirements for employment with the National Weather Service and satisfies the curriculum recommendations of the American Meteorological Society.

Audio Engineering Technology is a profession for those who want to be involved in the technical side of the audio and entertainment industry. AET students learn about the equipment, software and electronics that make music, film and television sound great. They also learn how to use these tools to create their own audio productions.

The Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology program prepares graduates to solve the technical and design problems that involve the creation, construction, and operation of automated systems. It provides students with a broad-based knowledge of engineering technology and automation systems with specific emphasis on robotics, sensors, industrial networking, and automation software.
Accreditation status: The Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Manufacturing Engineering Technology Program Criteria.
Program name: Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology, BS

description: The Aviation Management program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive background in the aviation industry. In addition to a core of aviation courses, the student will have a foundation in management, marketing, accounting, and finance. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers with airlines, airports, aircraft manufacturers, and government agencies. This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).
Accreditation status: This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

description: Biochemistry focuses on the chemical processes that occur in all living organisms. Biochemistry is the intersection of biology and chemistry. It is the study of life at the molecular level. This field has applications in many areas, including medicine, agriculture, and biotechnology. The Biochemistry major provides students with a strong foundation in chemistry and biology, as well as the specialized knowledge and skills needed for a career in biochemistry or a related field. Students have the opportunity to participate in research and gain hands-on experience in the laboratory.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB) and the Royal Society of Biology.

description: Biochemistry is the study of the chemical processes within and relating to living organisms. By controlling information flow through biochemical signaling and the flow of chemical energy through metabolism, biochemical processes give rise to the complexity of life. Over the last decades of the 20th century, biochemistry has become so successful at explaining living processes that now almost all areas of the life sciences from botany to medicine to genetics are engaged in biochemical research. Today, the main focus of pure biochemistry is on understanding how biological molecules give rise to the processes that occur within living cells, which in turn relates greatly to the study and understanding of whole organisms. This major is for students who want to work in the field of medicine, or in the biotech or pharmaceutical industries.
Accreditation status: American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB) approved

description: The minor in Biochemistry is available to any student at Purdue University, with the exception of students majoring in Biochemistry (BCHM) or Biochemistry (BIOL). A minimum of 15 credit hours are required for the minor. All courses must be taken for a grade. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses. Students must complete at least 6 credits of the minor in-residence at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.

Modern biology generates large amounts of data. This data needs to be effectively organized, synthesized and analyzed to advance the life sciences. The Bioinformatics minor is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the computational tools and methods used in this field.

Concentration name: Bioprocess Engineering, Cellular and Biomolecular Engineering, and Food and Biological Process Engineering
description: The Biological Engineering program is offered by the Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering. Students may enter the program through either the College of Agriculture or the College of Engineering. Biological Engineering is a field of engineering that focuses on the development and use of biological processes and materials to produce high-value products, to develop better processes for biological systems, and to manage biological systems. The Biological Engineering program at Purdue University is designed to provide students with a strong background in the biological and physical sciences, as well as engineering sciences. Students will learn to apply engineering principles to solve problems involving plants, animals, microorganisms, and biological materials. The program prepares students for careers in industries such as food processing, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and environmental management, as well as for graduate study or professional school in medicine or dentistry.
Accreditation status: The Biological Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Biological Sciences minor is available to any student at Purdue University, West Lafayette, with the exception of students majoring in Biological Sciences, Biochemistry (Biology), and Science Education (Biology). This minor is designed for students who wish to supplement their major with a background in the biological sciences and provides a broad overview of the field, from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems. A minimum of 19 credits in Biological Sciences is required for the minor. All courses must be taken for a grade, and a minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in the courses that are used to satisfy the minor. At least 10 of the credits must be taken at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.

This program, offered jointly by the Department of Biological Sciences and the College of Education, leads to the Bachelor of Science degree and eligibility for Indiana licensure to teach life science in grades 5-12. The program provides a broad background in the biological sciences, including a core of biology courses and additional biology electives, as well as the professional education courses and field experiences required for teacher certification.
Accreditation status: Purdue University’s teacher education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and the Indiana Department of Education.

description: The Biomedical Health Sciences (BMHS) major is designed for students who have a strong interest in biological and physical sciences and are interested in pursuing a career in medicine or another health profession (e.g., physician assistant, physical therapy, occupational therapy, dentistry, optometry, etc.). The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences, while also allowing students to take courses in the behavioral and social sciences, and the humanities. The BMHS major provides students with the flexibility to tailor their education to meet their individual interests and career goals.

Biometric systems are becoming increasingly important for identity management and person authentication. Biometric applications include person identification at borders, in secure facilities, on personal computers and cell phones, and in civilian and forensic investigations. Biometric systems are multidisciplinary and bring together topics from human factors, social and legal issues, hardware, algorithms, and databases. The biometric minor allows students to take courses that cover the fundamentals of biometrics and specialize in areas that focus on systems, algorithms and applications.

The Biotechnology Minor is available to students who have completed BIOL 11000 and 11100 (or equivalent) and CHM 11500 and 11600 (or equivalent). Students can earn the minor by completing 17-21 credit hours of specified coursework.

The Brain and Behavioral Sciences major is for students interested in the biological and health foundations of behavior. Core courses in the brain and behavioral sciences major provide a foundation in psychological sciences (e.g., developmental, social, and clinical psychology). Beyond these core courses, students focus their studies on the biological and health-related aspects of psychology through courses on the brain, learning, and health psychology. Research experience is a key part of the brain and behavioral sciences major, and students are required to complete at least two semesters of research. Our students go on to graduate study in psychology or medicine (e.g., medical school, physician assistant programs, or physical therapy) or work in various healthcare-related fields.

Virtual construction, also known as building information modeling (BIM), is the future of the construction industry. The building information modeling program teaches you how to manage the construction process and the construction site using 3D modeling and other technologies. You will use various tools to help owners, architects, and engineers visualize the construction project before construction begins. You also will use BIM tools to track and manage the progress of construction after it begins.

This minor is intended for students who are not majoring in any of the Daniels School of Business undergraduate majors. Students must complete 12 credits of Daniels School of Business coursework to earn a minor from the Daniels School of Business.

The Business French minor is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the French language and a comprehensive understanding of the business environment in the Francophone world. Students will develop their linguistic skills in French, focusing on the vocabulary and cultural knowledge necessary for professional communication.

Cell, Molecular and Developmental Biology (CMDB) focuses on how individual cells and molecules work together to create a living organism. CMDB students will learn about the mechanisms that control cell growth, differentiation, and communication. This program is excellent preparation for students interested in research, medicine, or the biotechnology industry.
Program name: Cell, Molecular, and Developmental Biology, BS

description: Chemical engineering is a discipline that is based on chemistry, physics and mathematics. However, it also includes aspects of other engineering disciplines, as well as the social sciences and humanities. A chemical engineer is someone who uses the principles of chemistry, physics, mathematics and other engineering disciplines to solve problems that involve the production or use of chemicals and other products. Chemical engineers are involved in many areas, including: research and development, design, manufacturing, and technical sales. The Purdue University School of Chemical Engineering provides a broad-based education in chemical engineering, preparing its graduates for a variety of careers in industry, government and academia.
Accreditation status: The Chemical Engineering (BSCHE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: A minor in chemistry provides a student with a broad range of knowledge in the various fields of chemistry. Students can gain experience in analytical, biochemistry, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry. The minor consists of five to six courses and is open to all students at Purdue who are not majoring in Chemistry or Biochemistry.

The Bachelor of Science in Chemistry degree is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous education in the principles and practice of chemistry. This program prepares students for a wide range of careers in industry, government, and academia, as well as for admission to graduate and professional schools. Students receive a strong foundation in the five major areas of chemistry: analytical, biochemistry, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry.
Accreditation status: This program is certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS).

description: The Chemistry (BSCHM) program is the professional chemistry major. It is specifically designed to prepare students for graduate study in chemistry or for a career in the chemical industry. This program is accredited by the American Chemical Society (ACS).
Accreditation status: Accredited by the American Chemical Society (ACS)

description: The Chinese minor is designed for students who wish to gain a solid foundation in Chinese language and culture. Through a sequence of language courses and electives in literature, linguistics, or culture, students develop communicative competence and a deeper understanding of the Chinese-speaking world.

The Chinese Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on Chinese language, literature, culture, history and society. You will gain proficiency in Mandarin Chinese and a broad understanding of the Chinese-speaking world through a variety of courses offered by the School of Languages and Cultures, and the departments of history, philosophy and political science. This program prepares you for careers in international business, government, education, and further graduate study.

Civil engineering is the oldest of the engineering professions. It is the field of engineering most directly related to the public and its welfare. Our society faces many challenges including: clean water, sustainable energy, traffic congestion, and failing infrastructure. Civil engineers deal with these and other issues. Our graduates are leaders in the development and application of advanced technologies to improve our infrastructure and the environment. The Lyles School of Civil Engineering at Purdue University is one of the most highly ranked and well-respected programs in the nation.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering degree program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Classical Studies minor provides students with an interdisciplinary introduction to the ancient Greek and Roman civilizations that are the roots of much of Western culture. Students take courses in ancient history, classical literature (read in translation), and ancient philosophy and religion.

Concentration name: Classical Languages; Material Culture and History
description: Classical Studies is the study of the languages and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome. The Classical Studies program at Purdue offers students the opportunity to study ancient history, literature, philosophy, religion, and art, as well as the Greek and Latin languages. Students in this major choose one of two concentrations: Classical Languages or Material Culture and History.

Concentration name: General Communication, Communication Management, Health Communication, Human Relations, Media and Mass Communication, Political Communication, and Public Relations and Strategic Communication
description: The study of communication is the study of how people use messages to generate meanings within and across various contexts, cultures, channels, and media. The Bachelor of Arts in Communication provides students with a broad understanding of communication processes and their impact on individuals, organizations, and society. Students develop strong written, oral, and visual communication skills, as well as critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
Accreditation status: The concentration in Public Relations and Strategic Communication is certified (CEPR) by the Public Relations Society of America (PRSA).

description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in music is a liberal arts degree. It is designed for students who wish to study music within the context of a broad-based university education. It provides a foundation in music theory, history, and performance.
Accreditation status: Purdue University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

description: The Computer and Information Technology (CIT) minor is available to any student outside of CIT who is interested in broadening their knowledge of the application of computers and information technology to their own major. Students gain basic knowledge of computing logic, systems development, information systems, and databases, and choose an upper-level elective based on their personal interest.
Accreditation status: The Computer and Information Technology program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET

Concentration name: Cybersecurity; Data Analytics, Technologies and Applications; Network Engineering Technology; Systems Analysis and Design
description: The Computer and Information Technology program provides students with a solid foundation in the principles and practices of information technology. The curriculum focuses on the application of computing technology to solve business and organizational problems. Students gain expertise in areas such as networking, cybersecurity, systems analysis and design, database management, and software development. The program emphasizes hands-on learning and prepares graduates for a wide range of careers in the IT industry.
Accreditation status: The Computer and Information Technology program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

description: Computer engineering is the design, development, and application of digital and computer-based systems. A computer engineer is a professional with a background in both electrical engineering and computer science. Such a professional is prepared to analyze and design computer hardware and software and to understand their trade-offs. The computer engineering curriculum includes courses in computer software and hardware, and it allows students to choose technical electives in several areas. Examples of these areas include computer architecture, operating systems, networking, communications, control systems, signal processing, and integrated circuit design. Students in this program are encouraged to choose a sequence of electives that will provide both depth and breadth in their area of interest.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET

description: The Computer Science minor is available to students in all majors except Computer Science and Data Science. Students must complete a set of core courses and then choose from elective courses that interest them.

Concentration name: Computational Science and Engineering, Computer Graphics and Visualization, Database and Information Systems, Foundations of Computer Science, Machine Intelligence, Programming Languages, Security, Software Engineering, Systems Software
description: Computer science is a discipline that involves the understanding and design of computers and computational processes. In its most general form, it is concerned with the understanding of information transfer and transformation. Particular interest is placed on making processes efficient and endowing them with some form of 'intelligence.' The discipline ranges from theoretical studies of algorithms to practical problems of implementation in terms of software and hardware.
Accreditation status: The Computer Science program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Lyles School of Civil Engineering offers a minor in Construction Engineering to students in the Schools of Engineering. The Construction Engineering Minor is designed for students who are interested in the construction industry and wish to enhance their engineering education with a focus on construction management and engineering.

Concentration name: Mechanical Emphasis, Electrical Emphasis, General Emphasis
description: Construction Engineering (CNE) is a unique program that blends engineering and management. Construction Engineering focuses on the design and execution of construction processes to create infrastructure. The program provides students with a solid foundation in engineering principles and construction management. Students will learn about structural design, construction materials, project scheduling, cost estimation, and legal aspects of construction.
Accreditation status: The Construction Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: Construction graphics is an important component of the construction industry. As modern technology advances, the use of graphics is essential to every segment of the industry. The construction graphics minor focuses on the graphical representation and communication of information between owners, designers, and contractors during the design and construction phases of a building project.

The minor in construction management provides an opportunity for students in other disciplines to gain an understanding of the management of construction projects. The minor is available to any student outside of the construction management major.

Construction management is the act of managing the construction process. It is a professional service that uses specialized, project management techniques to oversee the planning, design, and construction of a project, from its beginning to its end. The purpose of construction management is to control a project’s time, cost and quality. Construction managers are responsible for coordinating and managing people, materials, and equipment; budgets, schedules, and contracts; and the safety of employees and the general public. Construction management technology is a good fit for people who are interested in the construction industry, want to lead and manage people, and like to see a tangible result for their work. The Construction Management Technology (CMT) program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills to lead in the construction industry. The CMT program is management-oriented and provides a wide range of educational experiences, including both technical and management courses. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in many areas, including: building information modeling; construction graphics; construction surveying; materials and methods; scheduling; cost estimating; construction law; and structures. In addition to technical and management courses, the curriculum also includes courses in: communication; humanities; social sciences; and leadership. This well-rounded education prepares students for a variety of career opportunities in the construction industry.
Accreditation status: The Construction Management Technology program is accredited by the American Council for Construction Education (ACCE), 825 W. Bitters Rd., Suite 103, San Antonio, TX 78216. Telephone: 210.495.6161. Website: www.acce-hq.org.

description: The Creative Writing minor is designed to help students grow as writers of poetry and/or fiction. Students take a series of workshops and courses in literature and craft.

Concentration name: Poetry and Fiction
description: The MFA program in creative writing at Purdue is a three-year residency program. Its primary goal is to provide talented writers with the time and support to develop their craft. Students take workshops in fiction and poetry, craft classes, and literature seminars. The program also offers opportunities for students to serve on the staff of the Sycamore Review, our nationally recognized literary journal.

The Crop Science minor provides students with a foundation in the principles of crop production and management. It includes courses in plant science, soil science, and pest management, as well as elective courses in crop physiology, weed science, and crop ecology.

Concentration name: International Agriculture, Plant Breeding and Genetics, Crop Management
description: The crop science major is designed for students who are interested in the basic sciences related to crop production. Students in this major take a core of courses in chemistry, biology, mathematics, and physics. They also take courses in crop production, genetics, plant physiology, and soil science. The major is flexible and allows students to choose from several concentrations, including plant breeding and genetics, crop management, and international agriculture. Graduates of this major are prepared for careers in research, industry, and government, or for graduate study in the plant sciences.

The Cybersecurity major provides a comprehensive education in the technical and non-technical aspects of cybersecurity. Students learn how to design, implement, and manage secure information systems, and how to detect and respond to security threats. The program also covers the legal and ethical issues related to cybersecurity. Graduates are prepared for careers in a variety of cybersecurity roles, including security analyst, security engineer, and digital forensics investigator.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science program in Cybersecurity is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Cybersecurity and Similarly Named Computing Programs.

description: The Dance Minor provides students with a broad base of study in the field of dance. The required coursework involves the student in three areas: technique, theory/history, and performance. In addition to a core of required courses, students may choose to emphasize one area of dance more than others (e.g. technique, choreography, or history/theory) through their choice of elective courses.

The major in Data Analytics, Technology, and Applications (DATA) provides students with a strong foundation in data science, including statistical and computational methods, and their application to real-world problems. Students will learn how to collect, manage, analyze, and interpret large and complex data sets, and how to communicate their findings to a variety of audiences. The major is designed to prepare students for careers in a wide range of fields, including business, government, and non-profit organizations. This major provides a curriculum that integrates the areas of statistics, computer technology, and data science. Students will gain the skills and knowledge to manage, analyze, and interpret data to solve complex problems and inform decision-making in various industries. The program focuses on hands-on learning and practical application of data analytics tools and techniques.
Program name: Data Analytics, Technology, and Applications, BS

description: The undergraduate minor in Data Driven Agriculture will prepare students with the knowledge and skills to utilize data and information technology to improve the efficiency, productivity, and sustainability of agriculture and natural resources. This minor provides a foundational understanding of data science and its applications in the agricultural and natural resources industries. Students will develop proficiency in data management, analysis, and visualization, and will learn to apply these skills to solve real-world problems in agriculture and natural resources.

Data Science is an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from data in various forms, both structured and unstructured. Data Science is essentially a combination of Statistics and Computer Science. It is a field that is growing rapidly and has a wide range of applications in industry, government and academia.

The Design and Innovation minor provides students with the chance to engage in collaborative, design-based projects to identify and solve problems. This minor prepares students for careers and further study in a variety of fields, including: high-tech, business, non-profit, and education. It is open to students in any major, who want to develop their ability to communicate, innovate and lead. The minor is a partnership between the Honors College and the Purdue Polytechnic Institute, with additional contributions from the College of Liberal Arts and the Krannert School of Management.

Concentration name: Child Development, Family and Community Health, Human Development and Family Science
description: Developmental and Family Science is for students who are interested in people and in improving the lives of individuals and families. It is an interdisciplinary study of the development of individuals and families across the lifespan in various contexts. You will learn about the physical, cognitive, social and emotional development of humans and how to work with people in a variety of settings.

The Bachelor of Science degree in Digital Criminology is a joint program between the Department of Sociology and the Department of Computer and Information Technology. This program addresses the convergence of the physical and digital worlds, and how that impacts crime and its investigation. The program provides students with the foundational and specialized knowledge in both Sociology and Computer and Information Technology to analyze cybercrime and cybersecurity from a social science perspective.

The Digital Natural Resources minor is intended to provide students with a strong foundation in the use of digital technologies for managing natural resources. Students will learn to use geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, and other digital tools to collect, analyze, and visualize data related to natural resources.

description: The Early Childhood Education and Exceptional Needs (ECEEN) program focuses on the development and education of children from birth through age 5 (Pre-K). This program provides a strong foundation in child development and prepares students to work with children who are developing typically as well as those with exceptional needs. The curriculum includes course work in child development, early childhood education, and special education, along with extensive supervised field experiences. Students who complete the ECEEN program are eligible for Indiana licensure in both Early Childhood Education (Infant-Grade 3) and Early Childhood Special Education (Infant-Grade 3).
Accreditation status: The program is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).
Program name: Early Childhood Education and Exceptional Needs, BS
Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences Minor

description: Students in the ecology, evolution and environmental sciences (EEES) major learn to think like a scientist as they explore how nature works. They gain a solid foundation in biology, chemistry and physics while studying the environment at all levels — from the genes of individual organisms to the interactions of species and their roles in ecosystems. EEES students have the flexibility to customize their education by choosing from a wide range of elective courses that align with their career goals, whether they involve research, conservation, or environmental policy.
Program name: Ecology, Evolution, and Environmental Sciences, BS

description: The economics honors program is designed for students who want a more rigorous curriculum in economic theory and quantitative methods. It is excellent preparation for graduate study in economics, business, or law, and for professional careers requiring strong analytical skills.
Accreditation status: AACSB International

description: The Economics minor is intended for students who want to supplement their major with a strong foundation in economic theory and its applications. It is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of how markets work and how individuals and firms make decisions.
Accreditation status: Accredited by AACSB International

description: Economics is the study of how people make choices under conditions of scarcity and of the results of those choices for society. Economic analysis is a powerful tool used to understand how markets work, how people make decisions, and why some societies are wealthier than others. Students learn how to analyze data, how to think logically about complex issues, and how to communicate their findings to others. The BA in Economics is designed for students who want a broad education in the liberal arts and sciences, combined with a strong foundation in economic theory and applications. The program provides students with the analytical skills and knowledge needed for careers in business, government, law, and non-profit organizations, as well as for graduate study in economics, business, and other fields.
Accreditation status: The Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

description: Economics is the study of how people and societies choose to use the scarce resources that nature and previous generations have provided. It is a behavioral science that provides a toolkit for understanding and improving decision making in various contexts including finance, health, the environment and public policy. Economics is an excellent major for students who want a strong analytical and quantitative background to prepare for careers in business, government or for graduate study in economics, law or other fields.
The Electrical Engineering Technology minor is for students who want to develop their knowledge and skills in the areas of electricity and electronics.

The Purdue Polytechnic’s degree in electrical engineering technology (EET) is a hands-on, professionally oriented program that provides a combination of courses in electricity, electronics, and computers. You will learn to use computer-based design and analysis tools, work with state-of-the-art equipment in labs, and collaborate on projects with other students. The program provides a balance of theory and hands-on experience that gives you the skills needed to design, develop, and test electrical and electronic systems. EET graduates are prepared for a variety of careers, including electrical and electronics design, system integration, technical sales, and project management. They work in industries such as aerospace, automotive, energy, and telecommunications.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The School of Electrical and Computer Engineering offers two undergraduate degrees: the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) and the Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering (BSCmpE). Electrical engineering is a broad field that encompasses many diverse areas such as: Automatic Control; Bioengineering; Communications, Networking, Signal and Image Processing; Fields and Waves; Microelectronics and Nanotechnology; Power and Energy Systems; VLSI and Circuit Design. The BSEE degree provides students with a broad background in the theory and practice of electrical engineering, and the opportunity to specialize in one or more of these areas through elective courses.
Accreditation status: The Electrical Engineering (BSEE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Electronic and Time-Based Art Minor (ETB) is a multi-disciplinary area of study within the Department of Art and Design that is dedicated to the usage of electronics and digital technology in the production of contemporary art. While some classes are specific to a single genre, many take a cross-disciplinary approach. ETB studio courses cover such topics as computer programming for artists, physical computing, digital video, and art and technology history/theory. Students are encouraged to use these tools and concepts in ways that are investigative and experimental, pushing the limits of the media while creating work that is personally and socially relevant.

The Elementary Education program leads to a Bachelor of Arts degree and Indiana initial licensure in Elementary Generalist (K-6). The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the content areas they will teach, as well as the pedagogical knowledge and skills needed to be successful in the classroom. Students in the program complete a series of field experiences in local schools, starting in their freshman year and culminating in a full-semester student teaching experience.
Accreditation status: The College of Education at Purdue University is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

description: The goal of the minor is to provide students with the knowledge and tools they need to better understand the intersection of engineering and public policy and to apply their engineering skills to public policy problems. The minor is designed for students in engineering, but is open to all students at Purdue. This minor is intended to prepare engineering students for careers in the public sector, or for careers in the private sector that involve significant interaction with government. It is also intended to help all students understand the role of technology in public policy and the role of public policy in the development and application of technology.

The Engineering Technology Teacher Education (ETTE) program prepares students to become middle and high school teachers in technology and engineering education. ETTE graduates use a variety of laboratory facilities, and state-of-the-art equipment to apply math, science, and technology principles to solve real-world problems. ETTE graduates learn to design, build, and use various technologies to create products, systems, and environments that solve problems. Students are also prepared to teach in a wide range of content areas, including: Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Construction, Communication, Computer Systems, Design, Electronics, Energy and Power, Manufacturing, Robotics, Transportation, and Woodworking. ETTE students also participate in field-based clinical experiences in middle and high schools, and complete a 16-week student teaching internship during their final semester. Upon successful completion of the program, graduates are eligible for an Indiana REPA Initial Practitioner License in Engineering and Technology Education (Grades 5-12).
Accreditation status: The Teacher Education Program is a unit of the College of Education at Purdue University that is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and the Indiana Department of Education. The Engineering Technology Teacher Education (ETTE) program is also accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission (ETAC) of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The English minor consists of 15 credit hours in English, including introductory and upper-division courses. Students choose from courses in literature, creative writing, and professional writing to tailor the minor to their interests.

The English major provides students with a broad knowledge of literature in English and its historical and cultural contexts, as well as the ability to analyze and interpret texts and to write clearly and persuasively. The program offers a solid foundation in the study of literature, language, and writing, where students explore the diversity of human experience through the analysis of texts and develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills essential for a wide range of careers.

The Entomology major provides a broad background in the life sciences and prepares students for a variety of careers in the public and private sectors. Students study insects and their relatives, their roles in the ecosystem, and their impact on human health, agriculture, and the environment. The curriculum includes courses in insect biology, ecology, physiology, taxonomy, and management, as well as foundational courses in biology, chemistry, and mathematics. Students can choose from several areas of emphasis to tailor their degree to their interests and career goals.

Environmental and Ecological Engineering (EEE) is the multi-disciplinary engineering field that focuses on the protection of human health and the environment through the application of engineering and science. EEE uses a systems approach to solve environmental problems and minimize human impact on the environment. The EEE minor provides students with the opportunity to gain a broader understanding of the principles of EEE and their applications.

Environmental and Ecological Engineering (EEE) addresses the interactions between human activities and the environment. EEE engineers use engineering and science principles to design systems that protect human health and the environment, and to promote sustainable development. The EEE curriculum is uniquely designed to integrate traditional environmental engineering with ecological engineering and systems thinking. Students in the BSEEE program gain a broad foundation in engineering, biological sciences, and chemistry, and participate in design experiences that address real-world environmental challenges.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Environmental and Ecological Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Environmental Engineering and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

description: Environmental and natural resources engineers use their engineering skills to protect our natural resources. They design systems and solutions for environmental problems like water and air pollution, waste management and recycling, and sustainable food and fiber production. Environmental and natural resources engineering is part of the Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering.
Accreditation status: The Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Program name: Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering, BSENRE

Concentration name: Applied Biology; Environmental Quality; Environmental Policy and Management; Land and Water Resources; Sustainability Science
description: The Environmental and Natural Resources (ENR) major provides students with a broad background in the biological, chemical and physical sciences, and an understanding of the social, political and economic aspects of environmental and natural resource issues. Students choose one of five concentrations: Applied Biology; Environmental Quality; Environmental Policy and Management; Land and Water Resources; or Sustainability Science. In addition to a solid foundation in the sciences, ENR students develop skills in communication, problem-solving, and critical thinking that prepare them for a wide range of careers in environmental and natural resource management, policy, and research.

The Environmental Geosciences major provides a sound foundation in the Earth sciences and also incorporates a range of courses in biology, chemistry, and other areas of science. This major is intended for students who wish to pursue careers in environmental consulting, water resources, or other areas of the environmental sciences.

Concentration name: Environmental Health, Occupational Health Science
description: Environmental Health is the study of how our environment (air, water, food, and workplace) affects human health. Environmental health professionals use the latest technologies to identify, evaluate, and control chemical, biological, and physical factors in the environment that can cause disease or injury. Students choose from one of two tracks: (1) environmental health science or (2) occupational health science (industrial hygiene). Graduates in environmental health work as sanitarians, hazardous waste specialists, air and water quality specialists, and environmental health and safety (EHS) officers. Graduates in occupational health science work as industrial hygienists (identifying and controlling workplace hazards) or EHS officers. Both tracks prepare students for professional certifications, graduate study in environmental health or other health-related fields, or professional school (medical, dental, or veterinary).
Accreditation status: The environmental health science track is accredited by the National Environmental Health Science and Protection Accreditation Council (EHAC). The occupational health science track is accredited by the Applied Science Accreditation Commission (ASAC) of ABET.

description: The environmental politics and policy minor is for students who want to focus on the political and policy-making processes that shape environmental outcomes. This program provides students with the social science tools to understand environmental problems and the political and economic systems that impact environmental policy.

The Event and Meeting Management minor provides students with a foundational knowledge of the event and meeting management industry. Coursework focuses on the planning, management, and execution of various events including meetings, conventions, and festivals.

Exploratory Studies is an undergraduate advising program that provides students the opportunity to explore the University’s more than 200 majors before they commit to a specific degree-granting college or school. Students work with a professional academic advisor who is specifically trained to help them with the process of choosing a major. Students can remain in the program for up to four semesters. Students participate in the course EDPS 10500 - Academic And Career Planning, which is designed to help students evaluate their interests, skills, and values as they relate to majors and careers.

The Farm Management minor is designed to provide students with the business and management skills required to be successful in a production agriculture environment. Students will gain knowledge in the areas of farm management, production economics, farm business and estate planning, and farm business financial management.

The farm management major provides students with the management and economic skills to analyze the complex factors involved in farm operation and business. This major is well suited for students interested in production agriculture, professional farm management, or agribusiness. Farm management graduates often start their careers in farming, agricultural banking and finance, professional farm management, or retail agricultural sales.

The Fermentation Sciences minor provides a core of courses that introduce students to the field of fermentation science. Students will gain an understanding of the biology, chemistry, and processing associated with fermented foods and beverages.

The Film and Video Studies program (FVS) provides students with a solid foundation in the history, theory, and practice of film, video, and moving-image media. Students may emphasize either history and theory or production, though they are expected to take courses in both areas. The minor in Film and Video Studies complements many major areas of study at the university and offers students the chance to understand the cinematic arts as a form of cultural expression and global communication.

The Interdisciplinary Program in Film and Video Studies provides students with the opportunity to study film and video as art forms and as cultural phenomena. Students may choose from a wide variety of courses in film and video history, theory, and production. The program offers a major and a minor in Film and Video Studies.

Concentration name: Accounting, Analytical Consulting, Business Analytics, General Management, Human Resource Management, Marketing, Supply Chain, Information, and Analytics
description: Finance is the study of how people, institutions, and markets evaluate and manage risk and return. It involves a mix of conceptual analysis, quantitative math, and computer applications. The finance major prepares students for careers in corporate finance, investment management, and the financial services industry. Graduates can pursue careers as financial analysts, portfolio managers, investment bankers, and consultants.

The Financial Counseling and Planning program focuses on the financial planning process and its application to individuals and families. The program prepares students for professional careers in the financial services industry, including financial planning, counseling, and related fields. Students learn to analyze financial situations, develop and implement comprehensive financial plans, and communicate effectively with clients.
Accreditation status: This program is registered with the Certified Financial Planner (CFP) Board of Standards, Inc. and the Association for Financial Counseling and Planning Education (AFCPE).

description: A minor in Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences (FNR) is available to any student at Purdue University with an interest in the field. Students must complete a minimum of 18 credits from the list of courses below. A minimum of 15 credits must be taken at the West Lafayette campus.

Concentration name: Professional Flight Technology
description: The professional flight program is designed to prepare students for the flight deck of a major commercial airline. Flight students begin flying during the first week of their freshman year and proceed through several certificates and ratings including private pilot, commercial pilot with multi-engine and instrument ratings, and certified flight instructor with an instrument rating. At the completion of the program, students have the qualifications and experience necessary to meet the requirements of any commercial airline.
Accreditation status: The Professional Flight program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

description: A student may choose a minor in Food and Agribusiness Management. This minor will provide the student with an opportunity to supplement his or her major with a set of courses that provide a foundation in the management and marketing of firms in the food and agribusiness industry.

The Food Science minor is designed for students who are interested in the application of the basic sciences (chemistry, microbiology, physics, etc.) to the manufacturing, preservation, storage, and distribution of foods. The minor will provide students with the opportunity to gain a basic understanding of food chemistry and analysis, food microbiology, food processing and food product development. This minor is appropriate for students interested in careers in the food industry, research, and academia.

Food science is an applied science that uses the principles of chemistry, microbiology, and engineering to study the nature of foods, the causes of their deterioration, and the principles underlying food processing. Food science is also the application of this knowledge to the development of new food products and the design of new processes to improve the safety and quality of foods. Students learn the chemistry and microbiology of food, how food is processed, and how to ensure the safety and nutritional value of our food supply. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research, internships, and study abroad programs.
Accreditation status: The Food Science major is approved by the Higher Education Review Board of the Institute of Food Technologists (IFT).

description: The Foods and Nutrition minor is available to all students except those in the Nutrition Science, Dietetics, or Nutrition, Fitness and Health majors. A minimum of 15 credits is required. Courses used to satisfy the minor requirements must be taken for a grade. A minimum grade of C- is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor. At least 6 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette.

The Forensic Sciences minor is an interdisciplinary minor designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the various aspects of forensic science. Students will learn about the application of scientific principles and techniques to legal matters, including the collection, preservation, and analysis of physical evidence. The minor is open to all students at Purdue University.

The Forest Ecosystems minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the biological and physical processes in forest ecosystems and the management of these ecosystems for a variety of products and services.

The French Cultural Studies minor is designed for students who want to develop a deeper understanding of the French-speaking world, through its literature, cinema, history, and politics. This minor requires 12 credits of coursework beyond FR 20200.
The French Minor allows students to develop an intermediate-high level of proficiency in the French language and to gain knowledge and understanding of French and Francophone cultures.

A major in French at Purdue University gives you the chance to study the language, literature, and culture of France and the French-speaking world. In addition to developing proficiency in the French language, students gain a deep understanding of the history and cultural traditions of France and other Francophone countries. Students are also encouraged to study abroad in a French-speaking country to further develop their language skills and cultural understanding.

The Furniture Design minor is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of furniture design and construction. The minor is available to all students except for those in the Industrial Design program.
Accreditation status: The Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

description: The Game Development and Design major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the design and development of digital games. This degree program prepares students to lead the creation and development of digital games through the lenses of art, design, technology, and storytelling. Students gain a deep understanding of the diverse technical and creative processes involved in making games and learn how to apply those skills to various industries including entertainment, education, healthcare, and business.
