The General Education major is for students who are interested in the field of education but do not intend to teach in a P-12 classroom. This major does not lead to teacher licensure. Students in this major may be interested in working in education-related fields such as non-profit organizations, museums, corporate training, or other community-based organizations.

Concentration name: General Music Concentration; Music History and Theory Concentration
description: The Bachelor of Arts in General Music is intended for students who want a broad-based, liberal arts-oriented music degree. This degree provides students with basic musicianship, knowledge of music history and literature, and performance experience. It allows for flexibility in the choice of music electives and is ideal for students who wish to double major or minor in another area of study.
Accreditation status: The Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD) and the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

description: Genetics is the study of heredity. It is the core of biology, influencing the structure and function of every living cell. Understanding how genetics works is essential to understanding the complexities of life itself. The genetics major is for students interested in how genes influence the development, health and characteristics of organisms. The genetics program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of genetics and their application to a wide variety of biological problems. Students study a wide range of topics, from the molecular structure of genes and genomes to the inheritance patterns in individuals and populations. Graduates are prepared for careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and more.

Geology and geophysics is the study of the solid earth and the processes that shape it. The Geology and Geophysics major provides a broad foundation in the physical sciences and mathematics, with an emphasis on the study of the Earth’s composition, structure, and history. Students learn to use a variety of tools and techniques to investigate geological and geophysical problems, and to apply their knowledge to a wide range of practical and societal issues, such as natural hazards, resource management, and environmental protection. The curriculum includes classroom, laboratory, and field experiences that prepare students for careers in the energy and mineral industries, environmental consulting, government agencies, and for graduate study.

German remains an important language of international business, research, and culture. A minor in German will help you gain proficiency in the language and familiarize you with the culture and history of the German-speaking world.

The German major offers students the opportunity to gain a high level of proficiency in the German language while also exploring the literature, culture, and history of German-speaking countries. Our courses cover a wide range of topics, including medieval literature, Enlightenment philosophy, 19th-century realism, modernism, and contemporary German culture. Students are encouraged to study abroad in a German-speaking country to further enhance their language skills and cultural understanding. Graduates with a degree in German pursue careers in a variety of fields, including education, international business, government, and non-profit organizations.

Purdue University’s Global Engineering Studies Minor is a cross-disciplinary program that is intended for students who wish to supplement their primary engineering major with a set of courses and international experiences that will help to prepare them for professional practice in an increasingly global environment. Students should have a minimum of 3.0 GPA to be admitted into the program. Students may use up to six credits of engineering-related courses taken during an international study or work experience toward their primary engineering degree with the approval of their degree-granting program.

The Global Food and Agriculture Systems minor is an interdisciplinary minor available to all students at Purdue University. The minor provides students with a broad understanding of the global food and agriculture system, including the economic, social, and environmental factors that shape it. Students will learn about the challenges and opportunities facing the global food and agriculture system and will develop the skills needed to address these issues in a variety of professional settings.
Program name: Global Food and Agriculture Systems Minor

description: The Global Liberal Arts Studies (GLAS) minor is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with the opportunity to explore international and global issues from a variety of perspectives.

Global Studies is an interdisciplinary minor designed to provide students with a perspective on the globalization of the world and its impact on the local, national and international community. This minor allows students to pursue their interests in the world as a single unit or system, the complex interrelationships of the people and nations of the world, and the multiple ways in which global processes occur. In short, it provides students with a global context for their disciplinary major.

Concentration name: Thematic or Regional
description: Global Studies is an interdisciplinary major that allows students to explore the ways in which people, ideas, and things have become increasingly interconnected across the globe. Students in the major gain a broad understanding of the historical, political, economic, and cultural processes that shape our world today. The major is designed to be flexible, allowing students to pursue their specific interests through a choice of concentrations and electives. In addition to coursework, students are required to complete a global experience, which can be fulfilled through study abroad, an international internship, or other approved activities.

Graphic design is the communication of information and ideas through images and text. At Purdue, the Graphic Design program prepares students for a variety of careers in the field of visual communication. Our curriculum focuses on the development of conceptual, aesthetic, and technical skills. Students learn to use a variety of media to create visual solutions for a wide range of problems. The program also emphasizes the importance of design history, theory, and criticism.
Accreditation status: The Patti and Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

description: The Health and Disease major provides a solid foundation in the basic sciences (biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics) while allowing students to focus on the study of health and disease from a biological perspective. Students learn how cells and organisms function in health and how these functions are disrupted in disease. This major is excellent preparation for medical, dental, or other health professional schools, as well as for graduate study in the life sciences.

The minor in History is available to all students in the University. Students from any major can enhance their education with a history minor, which provides them with the opportunity to study a variety of topics, periods, and regions while developing skills in critical thinking, research, and communication.

The study of history provides an essential basis for understanding the contemporary world. History students examine the diverse cultures and societies of the past, and they learn to think critically, research effectively, and communicate clearly. The Department of History offers courses in a wide variety of fields, including United States, European, Latin American, Asian, African, and Middle Eastern history. The History major is flexible, allowing students to pursue their own interests while developing a broad understanding of the past. History graduates are well-prepared for careers in law, business, education, government, and many other fields.

A minor in horticulture provides a foundation for students who want to integrate horticulture with other majors such as biology, business, education, communication, entomology, and landscape architecture. Students from all majors are welcome.

Concentration name: Horticultural Science, Horticulture Production and Marketing, Landscape Architecture, Public Horticulture, and Sustainable Food and Landscape Systems
description: Horticulture is the science and art of growing, marketing, and using finished ornamental plants, fruits, and vegetables. It is a diverse field with many career opportunities in production, management, marketing, education, and research. Students can choose from five concentrations: Horticultural Science, Horticulture Production and Marketing, Landscape Architecture, Public Horticulture, and Sustainable Food and Landscape Systems.

The Hospitality and Tourism Management (HTM) program provides students with a broad-based education in the management of hospitality and tourism organizations. The curriculum emphasizes the application of management principles to the hospitality and tourism industry, including food and beverage, lodging, tourism, and event management. Students gain practical experience through internships and professional development opportunities. The program prepares graduates for leadership roles in various sectors of the global hospitality and tourism industry.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Programs in Hospitality Administration (ACPHA).

description: The international study minor provides students with the opportunity to gain a global perspective on the hospitality and tourism industry. To earn the minor, students must complete at least 12 credit hours of coursework while participating in a Purdue-approved study abroad program.

The minor in Human Development and Family Studies is available to students in all colleges and schools of the University. It is designed for students who want a better understanding of human development and family life, but do not want to major in the field.
Program name: Human Development and Family Studies Minor

description: A minor in Human Resource Management (HRM) allows students to learn how to help organizations strategically manage their employees. HRM is the function in an organization that focuses on the recruitment of, management of, and providing direction for the people who work in an organization. The HRM minor provides students with a solid foundation in the concepts and techniques of human resource management, including staffing, training and development, compensation and benefits, and employee relations. The minor is a valuable addition to any major, as it provides students with the skills and knowledge necessary to effectively manage people in any organizational setting.

Human rights studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws upon a variety of methods and perspectives from the humanities and social sciences to investigate how humans have conceived of rights and how these conceptions have been implemented, ignored, or challenged throughout history and in the present. The minor is intended to prepare students to be informed and engaged citizens in a global society and to provide a foundation for those who wish to pursue further study or careers in law, public policy, non-governmental organizations, or international affairs.

The Human Services major is a Council for Standards in Human Service Education (CSHSE) accredited program. The human services major provides a strong foundation for students interested in working with children, youth, adults, and families in a variety of human service settings. Students develop knowledge and skills to provide services that help people through every stage of the life cycle. The curriculum covers individual and family development, professional ethics, family and community resource management, diverse family structures and functions, and communication skills. In addition to regular coursework, students take three semesters of supervised field experience, during which they apply their classroom knowledge in real-world settings. Students find employment in a wide range of settings, including community centers, mental health centers, residential treatment programs, child care centers, elder care facilities, and government agencies. The major also provides a solid foundation for graduate study in fields such as social work, counseling, psychology, and public health.
Accreditation status: The Human Services major is a Council for Standards in Human Service Education (CSHSE) accredited program.

description: The Industrial Design program prepares students for the professional practice of industrial design. Industrial designers create and develop concepts and specifications that optimize the function, value, and appearance of products and systems for the mutual benefit of both user and manufacturer.
Accreditation status: The Department of Art and Design is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

description: Industrial Engineering is the branch of engineering that is concerned with the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, materials, information, equipment, and energy. It draws upon specialized knowledge and skill in the mathematical, physical, and social sciences together with the principles and methods of engineering analysis and design to specify, predict, and evaluate the results to be obtained from such systems. Through their education and training, industrial engineers (IEs) learn to view any organization as a whole system. They focus on improving the way these systems function. Because their focus is on the entire system, IEs can be found in a wide variety of industries: health care, retail, manufacturing, finance, government, transportation, and entertainment.
Accreditation status: The Industrial Engineering (BSIE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

description: The Industrial Management (IM) program is designed for students who have an interest and aptitude for business management as well as a strong interest in a technical or quantitative area. In addition to the core business and economics courses, IM students choose a concentration in a technical or quantitative area (e.g., computer science, engineering, or science). This enables IM graduates to bridge the gap between a firm’s technical and management functions.
Accreditation status: All of the Krannert School of Management’s programs are accredited by AACSB International (the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

description: A minor in Innovation and Transformational Change (ITC) is for students who want to develop a mindset and tools for innovation and leading change within organizations. Students will explore multiple aspects of innovation, with focus on identifying opportunities, understanding users, creative problem solving, and design thinking. Additionally, students will develop skills for leadership, teamwork, and agility to effectively lead change. Students from any major can earn an ITC minor.

The minor in Insect Biology is intended for students who have an interest in insects but do not have the room in their curriculum for a second major. It can be tailored to meet your individual needs or interests, like forensic entomology, public health, molecular biology, or ecology. The program will help prepare students for graduate study or careers in many fields of biology, as well as broaden your appreciation for the most successful animals on Earth.

The Intellectual Property Law for Engineers minor is designed to provide engineering students with a basic understanding of the legal principles that protect technological innovation. Students will learn about the four main areas of intellectual property law: patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets. The minor is intended for students who are interested in pursuing a career in intellectual property law or who want to learn more about how to protect their own inventions and designs.
Program name: Intellectual Property Law for Engineers Minor

description: The Integrated Business and Engineering (IBE) degree program prepares students to solve problems at the intersection of business and engineering. This interdisciplinary program, offered jointly by the School of Management and the College of Engineering, provides students with a solid foundation in both business and engineering. IBE graduates will be well-prepared for careers in technical sales, supply chain management, operations, and product management, where they can bridge the gap between technical and business teams.

Integrated Digital Media (IDM) is an interdisciplinary major that focuses on the creative use of digital technology in art and design. IDM students learn to use a variety of digital tools and techniques to create interactive and time-based media, including web design, motion graphics, video, and sound. The program emphasizes a critical and historical understanding of digital media and encourages students to explore the social and cultural implications of their work. Integrated Digital Media students can pursue careers in web design, motion graphics, video production, game design, and interactive art.
Accreditation status: National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

Concentration name: Engineering Management, General Engineering, Health Solutions, Visual Design Engineering
description: The Interdisciplinary Engineering Studies (IDES) program is designed for students who want an engineering education but do not plan to practice engineering. Students in this program want to use their engineering background as a foundation for a career in another field, such as law, medicine, business, or education, or for students whose interests in engineering are not satisfied by one of the traditional professional engineering programs. The IDES program allows students to customize their education by combining a core of engineering courses with a concentration in another field. Students in IDES must choose one of the available concentrations or work with an advisor to create an individualized plan of study. The concentrations currently available in the Interdisciplinary Engineering Studies program are: Engineering Management, General Engineering, Health Solutions, Visual Design Engineering.
Accreditation status: The IDES program is not an ABET-accredited engineering program.

description: The Interior Design program is a professional degree program accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA). The program provides a rigorous curriculum that prepares students for the complexities of the interior design profession. Students engage in design studios that address a variety of project types, including residential, commercial, and institutional spaces. The program emphasizes the importance of design thinking, technical knowledge, and professional practice. Graduates are prepared to enter the workforce as entry-level interior designers or to pursue advanced studies in the field.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA)

description: The International Studies in Agriculture minor is an interdisciplinary program designed to help students better understand the international/global aspects of agriculture and the food industry. This minor will provide students with the opportunity to gain a deeper knowledge of the history, culture, language, and economic, political and social systems of other countries. It is intended to prepare students for careers in the international arena.

The Interdisciplinary Minor in Islamic Studies is intended to give students a multi-disciplinary perspective on the historical and contemporary formations of Islamic society and culture. The minor requires 15 credit hours of course work in Islamic Studies and related fields. Six (6) of these credits must be at the 30000 level or above.

The Italian program at Purdue University offers students the opportunity to study one of the most important and influential cultures in the world. Students gain proficiency in the Italian language and explore the rich tradition of Italian literature, cinema, and art history. The curriculum is designed to develop communicative competence and cultural awareness, preparing students for careers in international business, education, the arts, and more.

The Italian Studies major is an interdisciplinary program of study. In addition to a focus on the Italian language, students may choose from a wide variety of courses in art history, history, philosophy, and other areas.

Students must complete 15 credits of course work in Japanese at the 20000 level or above. No more than six credits of the 15 can be at the 20000 level. All courses must be taken for a letter grade and completed with a minimum grade of C-.

The Japanese major provides students with a high level of proficiency in the Japanese language, along with a deep understanding of Japanese culture, literature, and society. Students develop skills in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Japanese, and they explore the rich historical and contemporary contexts of Japan.

The Jewish Studies Program is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the history, culture, and religion of the Jewish people. The program offers a minor that is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of Jewish life and thought from antiquity to the present. Students take courses in a variety of disciplines, including history, philosophy, political science, sociology, and English.

Concentration name: Clinical Exercise Physiology, Health and Fitness Professionals, Human Movement/Pre-Professional, Sports Medicine/Athletic Training
description: The undergraduate major in Kinesiology provides students with a broad knowledge of the physiological, psychological, and sociological aspects of human movement. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for a variety of careers in health-related fields and for graduate study in kinesiology or other healthcare professions.

Landscape Architecture is the art and science of design, planning and management of the land. Landscape architects design environments that are beautiful, functional, and sustainable. They design parks and playgrounds, trails and greenways, urban plazas and corporate campuses, and large-scale regional plans. The professional program in landscape architecture at Purdue University is a five-year program leading to the Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture (BSLA) degree. The studio is the core of the program, where students are challenged with design projects that range from small-scale site designs to large-scale urban and regional plans. The program also includes a required one-year professional co-op experience, which provides students with the opportunity to gain practical experience in a professional office environment.
Accreditation status: The Landscape Architecture program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB).

description: The Department of Horticulture and Landscape Architecture offers a minor in Landscape and Turf to all students in the University. This minor is not available to students in the landscape architecture or turf management and science majors. This minor is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge of plants and their management in the landscape.

Landscape Management is a diverse and growing professional field that includes the design, installation, and management of residential and commercial landscapes. The Landscape Management minor is intended for students who have an interest in some aspect of the green industry and would like to learn more about the plants used in landscapes, how to select those plants and where to use them, and the sustainable methods for managing landscapes. The courses focus on the business of the green industry and the science of plant health and sustainable landscape management.

The Latin American and Latino Studies Program (LALS) provides students with an interdisciplinary understanding of the peoples and cultures of Latin America and the Latino experience in the United States. LALS offers a minor that complements a wide variety of majors in the humanities, social sciences, and professional fields. Our curriculum covers a broad range of topics, including history, literature, politics, sociology, and the arts. Through this minor, students will gain a deeper appreciation for the diverse cultural heritage of the Americas and develop a critical understanding of the historical and contemporary issues facing Latin American and Latino communities.
Program name: Latin American and Latino Studies Minor

description: The Law and Society minor provides students with an overview of the role of law in society and an opportunity to explore the relationship between law and other social institutions. The minor is designed for students who are interested in law and legal institutions, as well as those who are interested in social problems and social change.

The Law and Society major provides a broad-based liberal arts education and is an excellent major for students who are interested in law-related careers. The program is designed to provide students with a broad exposure to the study of law and legal institutions and to the relationship between law and society. The major is interdisciplinary and includes courses from several departments across the university. Students in the Law and Society major will learn about the role of law in society, the relationship between law and social change, and the ways in which law is used to address social issues.

The Learning Sciences in Educational Studies minor is designed for students who are interested in the study of learning, instruction, and technology. Students will explore how people learn and how to design effective learning environments in a variety of settings.
Program name: Learning Sciences in Educational Studies Minor

description: The LGBT Studies minor provides students with an interdisciplinary program of study that explores the historical, social, and cultural contexts of sexualities and gender identities. Students will learn about the diverse experiences and expressions of LGBT people, as well as the impact of heteronormativity and cisnormativity on society.

The Liberal Arts major is designed for students who desire a broad-based, liberal arts education rather than a specialized major. It provides a flexible curriculum that allows students to explore multiple disciplines in the humanities, social sciences, and the arts. Students will develop critical thinking, communication, and analytical skills through a diverse range of coursework.

Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguists examine how language is structured, how it is acquired, how it is used, and how it changes. Since language is a human phenomenon, linguistics is a social science. Since language is also a cognitive phenomenon, linguistics is a part of cognitive science. At the same time, because linguistics deals with the products of the human mind, it is one of the humanities. The linguistics minor is an interdisciplinary minor designed to introduce students to the field of linguistics and to its applications. To meet the requirements for the minor in linguistics, students must take 15 credits of course work, including LING 20100 (Introduction to Linguistics) and LING 31100 (Fundamentals of Phonology) or LING 31500 (Fundamentals of Morphology) or LING 32100 (Fundamentals of Syntax).

Linguistics is the scientific study of language. It seeks to answer such questions as: What do all languages have in common? How do languages differ? How do children acquire language? How does language change over time? How is language processed in the brain? Linguistics is an interdisciplinary field that draws on insights from many different areas, including psychology, philosophy, computer science, and anthropology. The linguistics major provides students with a strong foundation in the core areas of linguistics: phonology (the study of sound systems), morphology (the study of word structure), syntax (the study of sentence structure), and semantics (the study of meaning). In addition, students can choose from a variety of elective courses in areas such as sociolinguistics, historical linguistics, psycholinguistics, and computational linguistics.

The Management minor is available to students in all majors except those in the Krannert School of Management. Students must have a minimum of 50 percent of the credits (8 hours) for the minor taken at Purdue. A minimum grade of C- or higher must be earned in all courses for the minor. Students must have a 2.0 GPA in the minor courses to graduate with the minor. The program requires 15.00 total credit hours.

Concentration name: Accounting, Analytical Consulting, Business Analytics and Information Management, Finance, Human Resource Management, Marketing, Operations and Supply Chain Management, and Strategy, Structure and Organizations
description: The Management major provides students with a broad-based education in business and management, covering various functional areas of business. All Management students choose at least one concentration to develop depth in a specific area. Concentrations are available in: Accounting, Analytical Consulting, Business Analytics and Information Management, Finance, Human Resource Management, Marketing, Operations and Supply Chain Management, and Strategy, Structure and Organizations. Students may also choose to complete a second concentration or a minor to further tailor their degree to their career interests.
Accreditation status: The Krannert School of Management is accredited by AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

description: Manufacturing is an essential part of the engineering process that takes a concept and creates a physical product. This minor is intended for students in an engineering or technology program who have an interest in manufacturing.

The Marketing major provides students with the fundamental concepts and the analytical tools needed to develop and implement marketing strategies. Marketing graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in brand management, marketing research, professional selling, and retail management. Marketing consists of those activities that anticipate and satisfy consumer needs and wants through an exchange process. These activities include marketing research, product development, pricing, distribution, and promotion. The study of marketing is helpful for any organization that provides a product or service to a customer.
Accreditation status: The Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business).

description: Materials engineering is an interdisciplinary field that involves the study of the structure, properties, and processing of materials and how these factors affect the performance of the materials in various applications. The minor in Materials Science and Engineering is designed to provide students with a basic understanding of the field and to prepare them for careers in a variety of industries where an understanding of materials is important.

Materials engineering is an interdisciplinary field that investigates the relationship between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Materials engineers design, produce, and test materials for a wide range of applications, from medical devices and electronic components to aerospace structures and energy systems. The School of Materials Engineering offers a program leading to the Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering (BSMSE). The curriculum is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the structure, properties, processing, and performance of all classes of materials, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and electronic materials.
Accreditation status: The Materials Science and Engineering (BSMSE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description: The Mathematical Economics major is designed to provide students with the mathematical and statistical skills needed for graduate study in economics and for quantitative careers in business and government. It is a joint program offered by the Department of Economics in the Krannert School of Management and the Department of Mathematics in the College of Science.

The Mathematics Department offers several programs leading to the Bachelor of Science degree. Mathematics is the study of number, structure, and change. The basic major provides a solid foundation for those who want to use mathematics in another field, such as business, law, or medicine. The Mathematics major is also good preparation for graduate study in mathematics, statistics, or a related field. Students may choose from several different plans of study: Mathematics; Mathematics Education; Applied Mathematics; Business Mathematics; Mathematics/Computer Science; Mathematics/Statistics; or Operations Research.

Mechanical Engineering Technology (MET) is a broad field of study. It includes such areas as: design and analysis of machines and mechanisms; manufacturing and production processes; fluid power and thermal systems; and engineering materials and their applications. MET students learn how things are made and how they work. They learn to use computer-aided design (CAD) software, 3-D modeling, and advanced simulation tools. In addition to technical courses, students also take courses in communications, humanities, and social sciences.
Accreditation status: The Mechanical Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: Mechanical engineering is the broadest of the engineering professions, and its practitioners can be found in a wide range of industries including aerospace, automotive, energy, medicine, and manufacturing. Students take a common core of basic courses in math, science, and engineering followed by more specialized courses in areas such as thermal-fluid sciences, solid mechanics, and systems and controls. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences and engineering fundamentals while also allowing students to tailor their studies to their specific interests through technical electives. The program culminates in a two-semester capstone design sequence in which students work in teams to solve real-world engineering problems.
Accreditation status: The Mechanical Engineering (BSME) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Medical Laboratory Sciences (MLS) program provides students with a strong background in the biological and physical sciences and the specialized knowledge and skills needed for a career in medical laboratory science. Medical laboratory scientists perform a wide variety of laboratory tests used in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. The program consists of three years of pre-clinical study on the West Lafayette campus followed by a fourth year of clinical training at an affiliated school of medical laboratory science. Admission to the clinical year is competitive. Upon completion of the program, students are eligible for national certification.
Accreditation status: The clinical programs are accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS).

description: The Medieval and Renaissance Studies program is an interdisciplinary program of the College of Liberal Arts that draws its faculty from several departments: Art and Design; English; History; Interdisciplinary Studies; Languages and Cultures; Music; Philosophy; Political Science; and Theatre. It offers both a major and a minor in Medieval and Renaissance Studies. This program provides students with a broad and yet deep understanding of the two periods that were most influential in the formation of the modern world. It gives students an appreciation for the historical development of Western culture and its contact with the cultures of the Mediterranean and the Near East.

Mechatronics is the synergistic integration of mechanical engineering, with electronics and intelligent computer control in the design and manufacturing of industrial products and processes. Mechatronics engineering technology at Purdue University is a unique program that uses a problem-solving, hands-on, and project-based approach to teaching students. It is designed for students who want to be able to design, create, and maintain the complex systems found in modern manufacturing environments. This curriculum provides students with a solid foundation in the fundamental areas of mechatronics engineering technology, including circuits, electronics, motors and drives, robotics, programmable logic controllers, fluid power, mechanics, and product lifecycle management.
Accreditation status: The Mechatronics Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: Meteorology and climatology is the study of the earth’s atmosphere and the processes that cause what we know as weather and climate. Students are prepared for a variety of careers in weather forecasting, research, and data analysis. The curriculum meets the requirements of the American Meteorological Society and the federal government for employment as a meteorologist.
Accreditation status: The curriculum meets the requirements of the American Meteorological Society and the federal government for employment as a meteorologist.

description: Microbiology is the study of the smallest living organisms—bacteria, viruses, algae, fungi, and protozoa. Microorganisms are used in many ways, from the production of medicines to the cleaning up of environmental pollution. Students in the microbiology major study the role of microorganisms in disease, the environment, and industry, and the basic biology of these organisms.

The Military Science and Leadership minor is designed for any student desiring to improve their leadership skills and is mandatory for any student who desires to receive a commission in the United States Army. This minor consists of 18 total credit hours from the courses listed below.

The Multidisciplinary Engineering (MDE) program provides students with the opportunity to develop a custom engineering degree that is tailored to their specific interests and career goals. Students choose from one of several pre-defined concentrations or work with an advisor to create a self-designed concentration. MDE is for students who want to be engineers and need a curriculum that is not available in a traditional engineering discipline.
Accreditation status: The Multidisciplinary Engineering (BSMDE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The minor in Music History and Theory provides students with the opportunity to pursue an interest in music. Students will gain foundational knowledge and skills in music theory and aural perception, and explore the history of music through a variety of genres and eras.

Music theory is the study of how music works. It examines the language and notation of music. It seeks to identify patterns and structures in composers' techniques across or within genres, styles, or historical periods. In a broader sense, music theory also distills and analyzes the fundamental parameters or elements of music — rhythm, harmony (harmonic function), melody, structure, form, texture, etc. Any person who plays, orbits, or writes music is using music theory. Music theory provides a way to explain what a listener hears.
Accreditation status: The Department of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

description: The Native American and Indigenous Studies (NAIS) minor provides students with a program of study that centers on the histories, languages, cultures, and contemporary issues of Indigenous peoples. Students will gain an understanding of the complex social, political, and historical contexts that shape the experiences of Indigenous communities globally, with a particular focus on North America. Through interdisciplinary coursework, students will develop critical thinking skills and engage with diverse perspectives and methodologies related to Indigenous studies.
Program name: Native American and Indigenous Studies Minor

description: The Natural Resources and Environmental Science minor is available to students in all colleges of the university. It is designed to provide students with a broad exposure to environmental and natural resource issues.
Program name: Natural Resources and Environmental Science Minor

description: The Department of Naval Science offers a curriculum in Naval Science to midshipmen in the Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps (NROTC) and to other interested students. The curriculum includes courses in leadership, management, navigation, ship systems, and the history and evolution of warfare. The program’s objective is to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to serve as commissioned officers in the Navy or Marine Corps. The curriculum is also available to students who are not participating in the NROTC program but who have an interest in naval science.

This major provides a foundation for the study of the biological basis of behavior, and of the function of the various systems of the human body. Because it emphasizes biological, chemical, and physical principles, the major provides an excellent background for those planning to go to medical, dental, or other professional schools, as well as for those planning to go to graduate school in several of the biological sciences. For those wishing to enter the workforce after receiving the bachelor’s degree, there are opportunities in research, the pharmaceutical industry, and laboratory and clinical settings.

The minor in nuclear engineering consists of 12 credits of nuclear engineering course work as specified below. Students interested in the minor in nuclear engineering should apply through the School of Nuclear Engineering.

Nuclear engineering is the field of engineering that deals with the practical application of nuclear processes and radiation. These include the design, development, and operation of nuclear power plants for electricity generation and propulsion, the use of isotopes and radiation in medicine and industry, and the management of nuclear waste. The curriculum in the School of Nuclear Engineering is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences and mathematics, followed by courses in the fundamental principles of nuclear engineering. The program includes study in reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, nuclear materials, and radiation detection and measurement. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research projects and to gain experience through internships and co-operative education programs.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Nuclear and Radiological and similarly named engineering programs.

description: The School of Nursing program is designed to prepare a nurse who can function in a variety of health care settings. The program leads to a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) degree. The program consists of a minimum of 120 credit hours.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree program, the Master of Science in Nursing degree program, and the Doctor of Nursing Practice program at Purdue University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org). The School of Nursing is also approved by the Indiana State Board of Nursing.

description: This minor is available to any student outside of the Nutrition Science Department. To enroll in the minor, contact an advisor in your home department. Students must have a 2.0 GPA to enter and complete the minor. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue.

The nutrition science major provides students with a strong background in the basic sciences of biology and chemistry. Students explore how nutrients in food are metabolized and used by the body and the role of nutrients in health and disease. Students find that this major is excellent preparation for graduate study in nutrition or other biological sciences. The major also provides the prerequisites for admission into medical, dental, and other health-related professional schools.

Nutrition, fitness, and health is a major for students who are interested in the roles of nutrition and physical activity in the maintenance of health and the prevention of disease. Students focus on the roles of nutrition and exercise in the maintenance of health and the prevention of disease. This program is for students interested in careers in the health and fitness industry, such as health and wellness coaching, personal training, and corporate wellness.

Occupational health science is the science of anticipating, recognizing, evaluating, and controlling workplace conditions that may cause workers’ injury or illness. Industrial hygienists use environmental monitoring and analytical methods to determine the extent of worker exposure and employ engineering, work practice controls, and other methods to control potential health hazards. The program is designed to provide the student with the necessary background in the basic sciences, such as chemistry, physics, and biology, and in-depth training in the specialized areas of industrial hygiene.
Accreditation status: The Occupational Health Sciences program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Organizational Leadership minor is available to all students at Purdue University, regardless of their major. The program focuses on the human side of organizations, including leadership, supervision, human resources, and organizational behavior.

Organizational Leadership (OL) is a leadership-focused, business-oriented degree. Leadership is the process of influencing others to achieve a common goal. Our curriculum covers the practical aspects of leading people and organizations, with an emphasis on communication, team building, and strategic planning. The program is designed for students who want to develop the skills necessary to lead in a variety of organizational settings, including business, government, and non-profit organizations.
Accreditation status: Association of Technology, Management, and Applied Engineering (ATMAE); Accredited

description: The Peace Studies minor provides students with the opportunity to study the causes of conflict and the potential for peaceful solutions. Students explore the history of nonviolence, the nature of war, and the ethical issues involved in peace and justice.

The minor in Pet Food Processing is available to students in all majors at Purdue who have met the course prerequisites. This minor is intended for students who have an interest in the processing and manufacturing of food for companion animals. This minor is housed in the Agricultural and Biological Engineering Department.

The Bachelor of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences (BSPS) program is designed for students who want to work in the pharmaceutical industry in the area of drug discovery and development or to pursue graduate or professional school in a variety of fields. This program is not intended for students who wish to become a licensed pharmacist.

Philosophy, the oldest and most fundamental of the liberal arts, is the study of the fundamental problems of existence, knowledge, and value. Its primary aim is to help students think clearly and critically about these problems and to express their thoughts precisely and effectively. The minor in philosophy is designed to provide students with a broad introduction to the field and its history, while allowing them to pursue their own interests in specific areas of philosophy. The program is available to students in all colleges of the University and requires 15.00 total credits.

Philosophy is the search for a clear and comprehensive understanding of the universe and of the human condition. It is an attempt to define and think through the basic problems of life and to see how they are related. Philosophy asks about the nature of truth and knowledge, of right and wrong, of God, of the relation of mind and body, and of the individual and society. Philosophy is excellent preparation for many professions, including law, medicine, teaching, and business.

Concentration name: Applied Physics, Astrophysics, Honors Physics, Physics Education, Physics
description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers several programs of study leading to the degree of Bachelor of Science. These programs are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of physics and astronomy, as well as the mathematical and analytical skills necessary for a wide range of careers in research, industry, and education.

Planetary Science is the study of the origin and evolution of the solar system and its component parts. This includes planets, moons, asteroids, comets, and meteorites. This degree program provides students with a strong background in physics and mathematics, as well as a broad understanding of the Earth and the solar system.

Plant biology is an area of study that provides students with a detailed understanding of the biology of plants and their importance in the world. Plant biology research and education includes the study of plants at all levels of organization, from the molecular to the ecosystem levels. Areas of research include physiology, genetics, development, and evolution. To explore these issues, students complete a range of courses in chemistry and biology, as well as plant-specific courses.

This major focuses on the plant sciences and develops the skills needed for the genetics, breeding and biotechnology industries. Students learn about genetic control and the manipulation of plant traits, the molecular biology of plants, and the application of these to the improvement of crops for food, fuel and fiber. This program prepares students for positions in the seed and biotechnology industries or for graduate study.
Program name: Plant Genetics, Breeding, and Biotechnology, BS

description: The minor in Plant Pathology is available to any student at Purdue University. The minor is designed for students who want to learn more about the causes and management of plant diseases. Students will learn about the biology of plant pathogens, the interactions between plants and pathogens, and the strategies used to control plant diseases.

The Department of Political Science offers a minor in political science to students who want to explore how we are governed, how public policy is made, and how we can be more effective citizens. The minor in political science is designed to provide students with an understanding of political systems, behavior, and policy. It is an excellent complement to majors in business, communication, history, and many other fields.

Concentration name: American Government and Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, Political Theory, Public Policy and Public Administration
description: Political science is the study of how people make collective decisions. It is the study of power and how we decide who gets what, when, and how. Political scientists study the exercise of power and how power can be used to improve the lives of citizens. In political science courses, you will learn how governments are organized and how political systems work, and you will learn about the role that ordinary citizens play in shaping those systems. You will learn about the major problems and challenges that different societies and the international community face and how we can best go about solving them. You will learn how to analyze political and social data and how to evaluate competing arguments about politics and public policy.
The Portuguese minor is designed to provide students with a basic proficiency in the language and an introduction to the cultures and literatures of the Luso-Brazilian world.

Pre-Communication is a non-degree granting program for students who intend to pursue a major in the Brian Lamb School of Communication. Upon completion of pre-communication requirements, students may apply to a major in Communication.

Dental schools seek students who have a strong foundation in the sciences, as well as those who are well-rounded and have demonstrated a commitment to service and leadership. Admission to dental school is highly competitive, and students are encouraged to seek the advice of a pre-professional advisor in the Center for Career Opportunities (CCO) Pre-Professional Advising office (Young Hall, Room 132; 765-494-3981). Pre-dentistry is not a major; students must choose a degree-granting major and complete the specific courses required by the dental schools they plan to attend.

Purdue University has long provided a superior background for students who go on to law school. There is no specific pre-law major at Purdue. Law schools do not require a specific major. Instead, they seek students with diverse backgrounds who have developed the necessary skills and have an excellent undergraduate academic record. Students with a serious interest in law should consult with an advisor in their major and the pre-law advisor for assistance in choosing a major and elective courses that will help prepare them for the study of law. It is important to remember that most students find success in law school after completing a degree in an area in which they have a genuine interest. Students with questions about pre-law should contact the Center for Career Opportunities (CCO), Pre-Professional Advising at (765) 494-3981 or by email at preprofessional@purdue.edu.

Preparation for medical school requires strong academic performance, as well as significant experience in a health care setting and a history of community service and leadership. There is no “pre-med” major at Purdue. Most pre-medical students choose a major in the College of Science or the College of Health and Human Sciences. However, medical schools accept any major as long as the student has completed the required science and math courses. Common majors include biology, chemistry, and brain and behavioral sciences, but students can also choose majors such as engineering, nutrition, or even the humanities.

The Pre-Nursing (PNUR) program is a one-year (two semester) program for students who intend to apply to the professional Nursing program. Pre-Nursing students apply to the Nursing program during their second semester of study for a possible start in the Nursing program in their sophomore year.

This two-year non-degree program provides the prerequisite course work required for application to Purdue’s four-year professional Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) program. Students who complete the two-year program are also eligible to apply to other pharmacy schools. Course work includes chemistry, biology, mathematics, physics, and communication, as well as several elective courses. After completing the pre-pharmacy requirements, students apply for admission to the professional program. Admission to the Pharm.D. program is competitive and is based on a student’s academic record, letters of recommendation, and an interview. Pre-pharmacy students are eligible to join the Pre-Pharmacy Club and the professional pharmacy fraternities.

The Pre-Physical Therapy program at Purdue is not a major; rather, it is a set of prerequisites that prepares students for admission to a doctor of physical therapy (DPT) program. Students can choose any major they wish as long as they complete the required courses for physical therapy school. Common majors for students interested in physical therapy include Kinesiology, Health and Disease, and Brain and Behavioral Sciences. Most physical therapy programs require a bachelor's degree before entry. Students should work closely with their academic advisors to ensure they are meeting the requirements for both their chosen major and the physical therapy programs to which they intend to apply.

Physician assistants (PAs) are health care professionals licensed to practice medicine with physician supervision. PAs provide a broad range of diagnostic and therapeutic services. A PA’s practice may also include education, research, and administrative services. PA education is based on the medical model. Physician assistant programs are typically master’s level programs and generally 24-27 months in length. The first year of the program is didactic (classroom) and the second year consists of clinical rotations. PAs are found in all areas of medicine including primary care and family medicine, emergency medicine, surgery, and psychiatry. For more information, please visit the Pre-Professional Advising website: https://www.purdue.edu/preprofessional/

The College of Veterinary Medicine offers a pre-veterinary medicine program for students who wish to complete the requirements for admission to the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) program. Students may follow the pre-veterinary medicine program in either the College of Agriculture or the College of Science. Students may enter the professional DVM program after completing a minimum of 70 semester credits of pre-veterinary course work. Most students, however, complete a bachelor’s degree before entering the professional program. Students who are interested in the pre-veterinary medicine program should consult with an academic advisor in the College of Agriculture or the College of Science.

The Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) minor provides students with a foundational understanding of the processes and tools used in industry to manage a product from its initial conception, through design and manufacture, to service and disposal. The PLM minor is intended to provide students with a cross-functional perspective of the product development process and the role of PLM in the modern enterprise. Students will learn about the business processes, organizational structures, and information technology systems used to manage product-related information and to support collaboration across the extended enterprise.

The Professional Writing minor (PWRT) is an interdisciplinary minor offered by the Department of English. It is designed to help students across the University develop the writing and communication skills they will need in their careers. Students in the minor learn to write for various audiences, purposes, and contexts, and to use various media and technologies to produce effective professional documents.

Professional writing is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for careers as writers, editors, and designers in diverse fields such as publishing, technology, business, law, and non-profit organizations. Students in the program learn how to communicate effectively with different audiences using a variety of media and technologies.

Psychological Sciences is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. It is a diverse field that includes many areas of study. At Purdue, the Department of Psychological Sciences offers two undergraduate majors: the Bachelor of Science (BS) and the Bachelor of Arts (BA). Both majors provide students with a strong foundation in the core areas of psychology, including clinical, cognitive, developmental, industrial-organizational, mathematical and computational, neuroscience and behavior, and social psychology. The BA degree is designed for students who want a broad education in psychology and may be interested in pursuing careers in fields such as business, law, or social services. The BS degree is designed for students who want a more intensive science-based education in psychology and may be interested in pursuing careers in research or healthcare.

Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. The Psychological Sciences major provides students with a broad foundation in the core areas of psychology, including clinical, cognitive, developmental, industrial-organizational, learning and memory, neuroscience, and social psychology. The curriculum emphasizes the development of research and analytical skills, as well as an understanding of the biological, social, and environmental factors that influence behavior. The major prepares students for a variety of careers in fields such as human services, business, and research, as well as for graduate study in psychology or related areas.

Concentration name: Health Policy and Management, Health Promotion and Education
description: The Public Health major provides a multidisciplinary approach to protect and improve the health of people and their communities. Students are prepared to address health challenges through education, promotion of healthy lifestyles, and research for disease and injury prevention. This major provides students with the foundational knowledge and skills to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate public health programs. Students also gain experience in public health policy, ethics, and environmental health. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for entry-level positions in public health or for further graduate or professional study.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Public Health (BSPH) is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

description: Public Relations and Strategic Communication majors focus on the way organizations communicate with their internal and external audiences to build and maintain mutually beneficial relationships. Public relations and strategic communication is practiced in almost every segment of society including corporations, non-profits, government, health care, and sports. Students gain foundational knowledge and skills in theory, research, writing, ethics and strategy. Practical experience is gained through a mandatory internship and opportunities to work in the student-run firm, Boiler Communication. After graduation, students pursue a wide range of career paths as account executives, media relations specialists, social media managers, public information officers and corporate communication managers.
Program name: Public Relations and Strategic Communication, BA

description: The Quantitative Biology major provides students with a strong background in mathematics and physics, while also providing them with a solid foundation in the biological sciences. This program is designed for students who want to apply quantitative methods to biological problems and for those who wish to pursue graduate study in quantitative biology, biophysics, bioinformatics, or related fields.

The Radiological Health Sciences minor provides students with a foundational knowledge of the physics and biology of radiation, as well as the safety principles and regulations related to its use in medical, industrial, and research settings. Students will learn about radiation detection and measurement, radiation protection, and the biological effects of ionizing radiation.

Concentration name: Medical Physics
description: The Medical Physics concentration in Radiological Health Sciences provides students with the prerequisite knowledge for entering an accredited graduate program in Medical Physics or related areas. This concentration prepares students for a career in clinical medical physics or medical physics research. It emphasizes the application of physics and mathematics to the diagnosis and treatment of human disease, particularly in the use of radiation for medical imaging and cancer therapy. Students take courses in biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics, as well as specialized courses in radiological health, medical physics, and imaging sciences.

Concentration name: Health Physics
description: Radiological Health Sciences (RHS) includes the Health Physics (HP) and Pre-Medical Physics (PMP) majors. These concentrations focus on the effects of radiation on living things and the environment. Health physics is a profession devoted to the protection of people and their environment from potential radiation hazards, while making it possible to enjoy the beneficial uses of radiation. Students find employment as health physicists in areas such as: medical facilities, national laboratories, state and federal government agencies, nuclear power plants, and industrial organizations. This major also provides a foundation for graduate study in Health Physics or other radiological sciences. The Health Physics (HP) program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Accreditation status: The Health Physics (HP) program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Real Estate program provides students with a solid foundation in real estate fundamentals, including valuation, finance, investment, development, and law. Students gain an understanding of the economic, social, and political forces that shape the built environment. The program prepares students for careers in various sectors of the real estate industry, such as commercial and residential development, corporate real estate, investment analysis, and property management.

Religious Studies is an interdisciplinary program that draws on many different departments in the College of Liberal Arts to offer students a multi-faceted approach to the study of religion. The Program’s offerings provide students with a cross-cultural and multidisciplinary perspective on the religions of the world and their impact on history, culture, and society. Students have the opportunity to investigate the origins and development of religious traditions, the roles of religion in the lives of individuals and communities, and the interactions of religion with other social systems such as politics, art, and law.

Concentration name: The Religion and Culture option, The Religion and Social Sciences option
description: Religious studies is a multi-disciplinary field of study that examines the history, literature, beliefs, practices, and institutions of religions. The program encourages students to investigate religion in its historical and contemporary contexts and to develop a critical understanding of the role religion plays in human life and society.

Retail management is a dynamic, fast-paced industry with a wide range of career opportunities. Graduates are prepared for careers in buying/procurement, retail management, merchandise coordination, and e-commerce. Retail management majors focus on the business of the retail industry. Students complete a common core of courses that provide a foundation in retail management, buying/merchandising, professional selling, and accounting/finance. These are complemented by coursework in economics, psychology, sociology, and communications. Practical experience is provided through a required internship.

Robotics engineering technology (RET) is a multidisciplinary field that combines mechanical, electrical, and computer engineering to create and maintain robots and robotic systems. Students in the robotics engineering technology program learn how to design, build, and program robots for a wide range of applications, including manufacturing, healthcare, and exploration. The program emphasizes hands-on learning, with students working in labs to build and test their own robotic systems. Graduates of the robotics engineering technology program are prepared for careers in a variety of industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, and defense.
Accreditation status: The Robotics Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

description: The Sales and Marketing major is designed for students who are interested in pursuing careers in professional selling, sales management, and marketing. The curriculum focuses on the development of skills in communication, problem-solving, and strategic thinking as they relate to the sales and marketing process. Students learn to analyze markets, understand buyer behavior, and develop effective marketing strategies. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in business and economics, with specialized coursework in professional selling, marketing research, and strategic marketing. Graduates are well-equipped to enter a variety of industries, including agribusiness, retail, and manufacturing.

Concentration name: Economics, Geography, Government and Citizenship, Psychology, Sociology
description: The Social Studies Education (SSED) program is an interdisciplinary major that prepares students for a career as a secondary (grades 5-12) social studies teacher. The program includes content coursework in history and other social sciences, as well as professional education courses. Students will develop a deep understanding of the social sciences and the pedagogical skills necessary to teach diverse learners in today’s classrooms.
Accreditation status: Purdue University’s College of Education and its educator preparation programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

Concentration name: Family and the Life Course, Health and Aging, Inequality and Social Justice, Social Control and Deviance, Social Organizations and Movements
description: A student may choose a general sociology minor or a concentration in one of the specific subfields: Family and the Life Course; Health and Aging; Inequality and Social Justice; Social Control and Deviance; Social Organizations and Movements. To earn a Sociology Minor, students must complete at least 12 credit hours in sociology, at least 6 of which must be at the 30000-level or higher. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. All SOC courses are eligible for the minor.

Sociology is the study of human social life, groups and societies. Sociology examines how our individual lives are influenced by our social environments, and in turn, how we change those environments. Topics of study range from small groups to global social processes. Sociology majors learn to think critically and analytically, communicate effectively, and identify and solve problems.

Concentration name: Environmental Quality, Soil Science, Water Science
description: Soil and Water Sciences involve the study of the physical, chemical and biological processes in the environment. Soil is the medium for plant growth and is a regulator of water flow and quality in the landscape. Students in the Soil and Water Sciences program apply their knowledge to solve problems of environmental quality, land use and management and agricultural productivity. In addition to a core of soil and water sciences, students choose one of three concentrations: Environmental Quality, Soil Science, or Water Science.

The Sound for the Performing Arts major provides a balance of technical and artistic skills through classes in music, theatre, and physics, as well as several specialized courses in sound and recording. Students get hands-on experience by running sound for several productions each year. Coursework covers live sound reinforcement, studio recording, and sound design for theatre. All students in the major must also complete the requirements of the College of Liberal Arts.
Accreditation status: The Department of Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).
Program name: Sound for the Performing Arts, BA

description: The Spanish for the Professions minor provides students with the linguistic and cultural skills necessary to communicate effectively in a professional environment. Students will develop proficiency in Spanish and gain an understanding of the cultural nuances that are essential for success in a global workforce.

The Spanish major provides students with high-level proficiency in the Spanish language and a deep understanding of the cultures, literatures, and linguistics of the Spanish-speaking world. Through a wide range of course offerings, students explore the diverse perspectives and histories of Spain, Latin America, and Spanish-speaking communities in the United States.

The Special Education Dual Licensure: Elementary Education and Mild Intervention P-12 program leads to the Bachelor of Arts degree and Indiana licensure in both Elementary Generalist (K-6) and Mild Intervention (P-12). Students must complete all courses with a grade of C- or better and maintain a 2.80 GPA to be eligible for licensure.
Program name: Special Education Dual Licensure: Elementary Education and Mild Intervention P-12, BA

Concentration name: Mild Intervention, Intense Intervention, Early Childhood Special Education
description: The Special Education Program is designed to prepare undergraduate students for licensure to teach learners with disabilities in preschool through grade 12. Graduates of the program are prepared to work with students who have various types of disabilities (e.g., learning disabilities, intellectual disabilities, autism, emotional/behavioral disorders, etc.) and their families.

Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences (SLHS) involves the study of the communication process, including its anatomical, physiological, and psychological bases, and communication disorders. The undergraduate program provides students with a broad background in the basic sciences related to speech, language, and hearing, as well as an introduction to the clinical aspects of communication disorders. Completion of the Bachelor of Science degree prepares students for graduate study in speech-language pathology or audiology, which is required for clinical certification and licensure.
Program name: Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences, BS

Concentration name: Applied Statistics
description: Statistics is the science of designing studies, and of collecting and analyzing data, for the purpose of helping people make decisions in the face of uncertainty. The study of statistics is much more than the study of mathematical proofs. It involves learning how to ask the right questions, how to design an experiment or survey to answer those questions, how to handle the data that is collected, and how to use the results to make decisions and provide insights. The Applied Statistics concentration is for students who want to apply statistical techniques to another field such as agriculture, computer science, economics, engineering, or health sciences. This concentration is a good choice for students who want a career in industry, government, or a non-profit organization.

Concentration name: Mathematics and Statistics
description: The Statistics major with a concentration in Mathematics and Statistics provides students with a strong background in both fields. It is specifically designed for students who may want to pursue graduate study in statistics or a related field. It provides students with a strong foundation in the concepts and tools of modern statistics and mathematics.

Concentration name: Art History, Ceramics, Drawing, Electronic and Time-Based Art, Metalsmithing, Painting, Photography, Printmaking, Sculpture, Textiles
description: The Studio Arts and Design (BA) degree is designed for students who want a broad-based education in the visual arts. Students in this program choose a concentration in one of several areas, including art history, ceramics, drawing, electronic and time-based art, metalsmithing, painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, or textiles.
Accreditation status: The Department of Art and Design is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

description: The Supply Chain and Operations Management (SCOM) major focuses on the management of business processes. These processes include the design, control, and improvement of business operations involved in the production and distribution of goods and services. SCOM professionals ensure that resources are utilized effectively and efficiently to meet customer requirements and achieve organizational goals.
Program name: Supply Chain and Operations Management, BS

description: Supply chain management technology (SCMT) focuses on the movement of goods and services from the source to the final customer. Global in scope, SCMT encompasses all activities associated with planning, sourcing, making, delivering, and returning products and services. To manage these processes, SCMT professionals use the latest technology to synchronize the flows of materials, information, and financial resources. The SCMT curriculum is designed to prepare students for leadership roles in various sectors, including manufacturing, retail, logistics, and consulting. Core courses cover topics such as procurement, operations, inventory management, transportation, and supply chain analytics. Students also gain practical experience through internships and industry-sponsored projects, ensuring they are well-equipped to solve real-world supply chain challenges.
Accreditation status: The Supply Chain Management Technology program is accredited by the Association of Technology, Management, and Applied Engineering (ATMAE).

Concentration name: Process and Product Design
description: Sustainable biomaterials (SBIO) students learn about the biology, chemistry, and physics of renewable, plant-based materials and how they are used for many of the products we use every day. Students study the science and technology that goes into converting trees and other plants into sustainable products, such as buildings, furniture, paper, and biofuels. The Process and Product Design concentration is designed for students interested in manufacturing, marketing, and the design and use of wood and other plant-based materials for construction and consumer products.
Program name: Sustainable Biomaterials-Process and Product Design, BS

description: The Sustainable Food and Farming Systems (SFFS) major focuses on the production of food, fiber and medicinal plants. The core of this major is an understanding of the ecology of farming systems, and the practices that result in high productivity while protecting the environment and supporting the local community. The curriculum includes plant and soil science, cropping systems, integrated pest management, and the business and marketing of farm products. This major is highly interdisciplinary and can be customized to your individual interests. It provides great preparation for careers in farming, agricultural education, consulting, greenhouse and nursery production, processing and marketing of organic and specialty products, and non-profit organizations focused on food security.
Program name: Sustainable Food and Farming Systems, BS
