description: The Systems Analysis and Design (SA&D) major in Computer and Information Technology (CIT) focuses on the development of computer-based information systems. The major provides a strong foundation in systems analysis, database systems, and project management. Students learn to analyze business and organizational needs and to design and implement information systems to meet those needs. Graduates are prepared for careers as systems analysts, business analysts, and project managers.
Accreditation status: The Computer and Information Technology program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Information Technology Program Criteria.

description: This program is designed for students who are interested in teaching physical education and health at the elementary, middle, and/or high school levels. Students who complete the program are eligible for an Indiana dual license in Physical Education (P-12) and Health (P-12).
Accreditation status: Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP)

description: The turfgrass industry is a multi-billion dollar a year industry with career opportunities in several areas including: golf course management, professional and collegiate sports field management, professional lawn care, sod production, and grounds management for municipalities, parks, and schools. Other opportunities include sales and marketing, research and development, and technical support within the turfgrass industry. The Turf Management and Science major is designed for students who are interested in a career in any of these areas. This major provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences of botany, soils, and chemistry, and also provides students with the specialized knowledge and skills needed to manage turfgrass systems. Students will also take courses in business and management to prepare them for the business aspects of the turfgrass industry.

The unmanned aerial systems (UAS) major provides students with the skills and knowledge to design, build, and operate unmanned aircraft. Students will learn about flight dynamics, control systems, sensors, and data analysis, and will have the opportunity to participate in hands-on projects and internships.
Accreditation status: The unmanned aerial systems program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International (AABI).

description: User experience (UX) design is a multidisciplinary field that focuses on the design of the interaction between users and products, such as websites, applications, and devices. The goal of UX design is to create products that are easy to use, efficient, and enjoyable for the user. Students in the UX design program learn about the user-centered design process, which includes research, prototyping, and testing. They also learn about visual design, information architecture, and interaction design. The program emphasizes hands-on, project-based learning, and students have the opportunity to work on real-world projects for clients.

The Veterinary Nursing Program (formerly the Veterinary Technology Program) provides students with the knowledge and skills required to become a veterinary nurse. The Veterinary Nursing Program is an integral part of the College of Veterinary Medicine. Veterinary nurses are an essential part of the veterinary medical team. Veterinary nurses perform many of the same tasks for animal patients that nurses and other professionals perform for human patients. Students learn through a combination of classroom, laboratory, and clinical experiences. During the clinical rotations, students work alongside veterinarians, veterinary nursing students, and veterinary nurses in the Purdue Veterinary Teaching Hospital.
Accreditation status: The Veterinary Nursing Program is fully accredited by the American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA).

description: Virtual Product Integration graduates are prepared to help companies build and improve their virtual enterprises. These specialists take digital product designs and add information and intelligence that allow a company to evaluate its lifecycle, manufacturing and performance. Students utilize 3D modeling, product data management (PDM), product lifecycle management (PLM) and other high-end software tools to create and simulate the entire lifecycle of a product from its initial concept to its eventual disposal.

The web programming and design major is for students who want to be involved in the design and development of the websites we use every day. Students will learn how to design, build and manage complex websites and web applications using the latest technologies and tools. The program is a collaboration between the Brian Lamb School of Communication and the Department of Computer Graphics Technology.

The Welding Engineering Technology program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive education in the application of welding technology, materials science, and engineering principles. The program emphasizes the practical application of welding processes, design, and inspection techniques. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in a wide range of industries, including manufacturing, construction, aerospace, and energy. Students in the WET program have access to state-of-the-art welding equipment and laboratories. They also have the opportunity to participate in internships and research projects with industry partners.
Accreditation status: The Welding Engineering Technology program is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The Wildlife major provides students with a broad background in the life sciences, plus specific knowledge in the ecology, management, and conservation of wildlife and their habitats. The curriculum is designed to meet the educational requirements for certification as an Associate Wildlife Biologist by The Wildlife Society. Students are prepared for careers with state and federal agencies, non-profit organizations, and private firms. Many students also pursue graduate degrees.

The Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Program (WGSS) offers an interdisciplinary undergraduate major and minor. In WGSS, we study the way gender and sexuality are shaped by and within political, social and cultural contexts. We study why social inequalities exist and how to make the world more just and inclusive. We think about gender and sexuality in relation to race, class, disability and nationality. We study diverse subjects—like politics, history, literature and media—to understand the complexity of human experience.
Program name: Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies, BA
